title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ وَشَمْسِ الدِّينِ
titleEn: Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn, continued: the Wedding Night in Cairo and Damascus
part: Night 22 · The Tale of Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 164–176 (Night 22, continuing directly from nights-21), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 22 continues the jinn's quarrel over whose beauty is greater: the ʿifrīt carries the sleeping Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan from Basra to Cairo, dresses him, and sends him into the wedding procession of the vizier's daughter, Sitt al-Ḥusn, whom the hunchback groom has been hired to marry. She rejects the hunchback for Ḥasan; the household learns of the jest, the hunchback is driven out, and Ḥasan spends the night with her. The jinn then carry him off again, leaving him at a gate of Damascus, where a cook takes him in. Verse is copied as printed, and pointed by us only where the print has no marks. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ قَٰلَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْجِنِّيَّ لَمَّا حَكَٰي لِلْجِنِّيَّةِ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ كَتَبَ كِتَابَهَا عَلَى السَّائِسِ الْأَحْدَبِ وَهِيَ فِي غَايَةِ الْحُزْنِ وَلَمْ أَجِدْ شَبِيهًا فِي الْجَمَالِ إِلَّا هَذَا الشَّابَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāniyatu wa-al-ʿishrūna qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-jinniyya lammā ḥakā li-al-jinniyyati anna al-malika kataba kitābahā ʿalā al-sāʾisi al-aḥdabi wa-hiya fī ghāyati al-ḥuzni wa-lam ajid shabīhan fī al-jamāli illā hādhā al-shābba
sentences.l: And-when was the-night the-second and-the-twenty, she-said: It-has-reached-me, O king the-fortunate, that the-jinni, when he-related to-the-jinniyya that the-king had-written her contract upon the-groom the-hunchback, and-she in extremity of-the-grief, and-not I-found a-like in the-beauty except this the-youth,
sentences.i: And when it was the twenty-second night, she said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the jinni told the jinniyya that the king had written the girl's marriage-contract to the hunchbacked groom, and that she was in the depths of grief, he added that he had found no match for her in beauty except this young man,
sentences.n: قلت is printed for قالت; it is read qālat, "she said" (Shahrazād). The last clause slips into the jinni's own first person ("I did not find"), a common looseness in reported speech. السائس is the groom of horses, the hunchback's trade, and so a low match for a vizier's daughter.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ الْجِنِّيَّةُ تَكْذِبُ فَإِنَّ هَذَا الشَّابَّ أَحْسَنُ أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِ
sentences.tr: qālat lahu al-jinniyyatu takdhibu fa-inna hādhā al-shābba aḥsanu ahli zamānihi
sentences.l: Said to-him the-jinniyya: You-lie! For-indeed this the-youth is-fairest-of the-people-of his-time.
sentences.i: The jinniyya said to him, "You lie! This young man is the handsomest of the people of his age."

sentences.t: فَرَدَّهَا الْعِفْرِيتُ وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ يَا أُخْتِي إِنَّ الصَّبِيَّةَ أَحْسَنُ مِنْ هَذَا وَلَكِنْ لَا يَصْلُحُ لَهَا إِلَّا هُوَ فَإِنَّهُمَا مِثْلُ بَعْضِهِمَا أَخَوَاتٌ وَأَوْلَادُ عَمٍّ يَاخَسَارَ تَهَامَعَ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-radda-hā al-ʿifrītu wa-qāla wa-Allāhi yā ukhtī inna al-ṣabiyyata aḥsanu min hādhā wa-lakin lā yaṣluḥu lahā illā huwa fa-innahumā mithlu baʿḍihimā akhawātun wa-awlādu ʿammin yā-khasāra tahāmaʿa hādhā al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: And-returned-her the-ifrit and-said: By-God, O my-sister, indeed the-girl is-fairer than this-one; but not is-fitting for-her except he; for-indeed-the-two-of-them are like each-of-them-two: sisters and-sons-of an-uncle. O loss! her-with this the-hunchback!
sentences.i: The ifrit answered her, and said, "By God, my sister, the girl is fairer than this youth; but no one suits her except him, for the two of them are as alike as sisters and cousins. What a pity, her with this hunchback!"
sentences.n: ياخسار تهامع is misdivided in the print. It is best read يَا خَسَارَتَهَا مَعَ, "O the loss of her, with ...": the -t- of خسارتها has slid onto the next word. The vocalisation keeps the printed division. أَخَوَات is "sisters", used loosely for "siblings"; أَوْلَادُ عَمٍّ, "sons of an uncle", are cousins.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَاخِي دَعْنَا نَدْخُلْ تَحْتَهُ وَنَحْمِلْهُ وَنَرُوحْ بِهِ إِلَى الصَّبِيَّةِ الَّتِي تَقُولُ عَنْهَا وَنَنْظُرْ مَنْ هُوَ أَحْسَنُ فِيهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu yākhī daʿnā nadkhul taḥtahu wa-naḥmilhu wa-narūḥ bihi ilā al-ṣabiyyati allatī taqūlu ʿanhā wa-nanẓur man huwa aḥsanu fīhimā
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: O-my-brother, leave-us, we-enter beneath-him and-we-carry-him and-we-go with-him to the-girl whom you-say about-her, and-we-look who he is fairest among-the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: And she said to him, "My brother, let us get beneath him, lift him, and carry him off to the girl you speak of, and see which of the two is the fairer."
sentences.n: دَعْنَا followed by a bare jussive (نَدْخُلْ ...) is "let us ...", "allow us to ...". The speaker is the jinniyya; "him" is the youth asleep on his father's tomb in Baṣra.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْعِفْرِيتُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً هَذَا كَلَامٌ صَوَابٌ وَلَا هُنَاكَ أَحْسَنُ مِنْ هَذَا الرَّأْيِ الَّذِي تَقُولِيهِ أَنَا أَحْمِلُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ʿifrītu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan hādhā kalāmun ṣawābun wa-lā hunāka aḥsanu min hādhā al-raʾyi alladhī taqūlīhi anā aḥmiluhu
sentences.l: And-said the-ifrit: Hearing and-obedience! This is-speech right, and-not there is anything fairer than this the-opinion which you-(f.)-say. I carry-him.
sentences.i: And the ifrit said, with hearing and obedience: "That is sound speech, and nothing could be better than this plan of yours. I will carry him."
sentences.n: سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً is the standard formula of assent, an accusative of the thing offered: (I give) hearing and obedience. تَقُولِيهِ has the feminine ending because the ifrit is speaking to the jinniyya.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ حَمَلَهُ وَطَارَبِهِ إِلَى الْجَوِّ وَصَارَتِ الْعِفْرِيتَةُ فِي رِكَابِهِ تُحَاذِيهِ إِلَى أَنْ نَزَلَ بِهِ إِلَى مَدِينَةِ مِصْرَوَحَطَّهُ عَلَى مَصْطَبَةٍ وَنَبَّهَهُ فَاسْتَيْقَظَ مِنَ النَّوْمِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu ḥamalahu wa-ṭāra-bihi ilā al-jawwi wa-ṣārati al-ʿifrītatu fī rikābihi tuḥādhīhi ilā an nazala bihi ilā madīnati miṣra wa-ḥaṭṭahu ʿalā maṣṭabatin wa-nabbahahu fa-istayqaẓa min al-nawmi
sentences.l: Then indeed-he carried-him and-flew-with-him to the-air; and-became the-she-ifrit at his-stirrup, keeping-abreast-of-him, until he-descended with-him to the-city of-Miṣr and-set-him-down on a-bench and-roused-him; and-he-awoke from the-sleep.
sentences.i: Then he lifted him and flew with him up into the air, while the she-ifrit kept at his stirrup, flying level with him, until he came down with him in the city of Miṣr, set him on a bench, and roused him; and he woke from his sleep.
sentences.n: Two words are run together in the print: وطاربه (وَطَارَ بِهِ) and مصروحطه (مِصْرَ وَحَطَّهُ). مدينة مصر, "the city of Miṣr", is Cairo. فِي رِكَابِهِ is literally "in his stirrup", that is, at his side.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَجِدْ نَفْسَهُ عَلَٰي قَبْرِ أَبِيهِ فِي أَرْضِ الْبَصْرَةِ فَنَظَرَ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا لَايَجِدُ نَفْسَهُ إِلَّا فِي مَدِينَةٍ غَيْرِ مَدِينَةِ الْبَصْرَةِ فَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَعِيطَ فَوَكَزَهُ الْعِفْرِيتُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yajid nafsahu ʿalā qabri abīhi fī arḍi al-baṣrati fa-naẓara yamīnan wa-shimālan lā-yajidu nafsahu illā fī madīnatin ghayri madīnati al-baṣrati fa-arāda an yaʿīṭa fa-wakazahu al-ʿifrītu
sentences.l: And-not he-found himself upon the-grave of-his-father in the-land of-al-Baṣra. So-he-looked right and-left, not-he-finds himself except in a-city other-than the-city of-al-Baṣra; so-he-wished that he-cry-out; and-jabbed-him the-ifrit.
sentences.i: He found that he was no longer upon his father's grave in the land of Basra. He looked right and left and found himself only in a city other than Basra, and he wished to cry out; but the ifrit gave him a jab.
sentences.n: يَعِيطَ is colloquial (Egyptian) "to shout, cry out". لَايَجِدُ is printed as one word; it is the present "he finds" after a negative, with the sense "and he could find himself nowhere but ...". علي is printed for على and carries the dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْعِفْرِيتُ قَدْ أَتَى لَهُ بِحُلَّةٍ فَاخِرَةٍ وَأَلْبَسَهُ إِيَّاهَا وَأَوْقَدَ لَهُ شَمْعَةً وَقَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَنِّي جِبْتُكَ وَأَنَا رَائِحٌ أَعْمَلُ مَعَكَ شَيْئًا لِلَّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-ʿifrītu qad atā lahu bi-ḥullatin fākhiratin wa-albasahu iyyāhā wa-awqada lahu shamʿatan wa-qāla lahu iʿlam annī jibtuka wa-anā rāʾiḥun aʿmalu maʿaka shayʾan li-Allāhi
sentences.l: And-was the-ifrit had brought for-him, with a-robe splendid, and-clothed-him it, and-lit for-him a-candle, and-said to-him: Know that-I I-brought-you, and-I going, I-do with-you a-thing for-God.
sentences.i: The ifrit had brought him a splendid robe, dressed him in it, and lit a candle for him. And he said to him, "Know that I have brought you here, and I am about to do something with you for God's sake."
sentences.n: جِبْتُكَ is the colloquial "I brought you" (Classical جِئْتُكَ). رَائِحٌ is "going", and with a following verb "about to". أَتَى لَهُ بِـ is "brought him ...": أَتَى takes بِـ for the thing brought.

sentences.t: فَخُذْ هَذِهِ الشَّمْعَةَ وَامْشِ إِلَى ذَلِكَ الْحَمَّامِ وَاخْتَلِطْ بِالنَّاسِ، وَلَا تَنْزِلْ تَمْشِي مَعَهُمْ إِلَى أَنْ تَصِلَ إِلَى قَاعَةِ الْعَرُوسَةِ فَاسْبِقْ وَادْخُلِ الْقَاعَةَ وَلَمْ تَخْشَ أَحَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-khudh hādhihi al-shamʿata wa-imshi ilā dhālika al-ḥammāmi wa-ikhtaliṭ bi-al-nāsi, wa-lā tanzil tamshī maʿahum ilā an taṣila ilā qāʿati al-ʿarūsati fa-asbiq wa-udkhuli al-qāʿata wa-lam takhsha aḥadan
sentences.l: So take this the-candle and-walk to that the-bath-house and-mingle with-the-people, and-do-not descend; you-walk with-them until you-arrive at the-hall of-the-bride; then-get-ahead and-enter the-hall, and-not you-fear anyone.
sentences.i: Take this candle, walk to that bathhouse, and mingle with the crowd, and do not fall out of step but keep walking with them until you reach the bride's hall. Then press ahead, enter the hall, and fear no one.
sentences.n: وَلَمْ تَخْشَ احدا is a negative command in the shape of a past-tense negation (لم + jussive), which Classical Arabic would write with لَا. The bathhouse is where a bridegroom's procession sets out from. لَا تَنْزِلْ تَمْشِي is literally "do not come down, you walk", that is, do not drop out of the walking.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ مِثْلَ مَا دَخَلْتَ فَقِفْ فَوْقَ يَمِينِ الْعَرِيسِ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-anta mithla mā dakhalta fa-qif fawqa yamīni al-ʿarīsi al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: And-you, like what you-entered, stand above the-right of-the-bridegroom the-hunchback.
sentences.i: And as soon as you enter, take your stand above the hunchbacked bridegroom, on his right.
sentences.n: مِثْلَ مَا is "just as", "as soon as". فَوْقَ يَمِينِ is "above (higher than) the right side": the place of honour at the groom's right.

sentences.t: وَكُلَّ مَاجَاءَ كَ الْمَوَاشِطُ وَالْمَغَانِي وَالدَّايَاتُ حُطَّ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَجِدْهُ مَلْآنَ ذَهَبٍ فَاكْمُشْ وَارْمِ لَهُمْ وَلَاتَتَوَهَّمْ أَنَّكَ لَاتُدْخِلُ يَدَكَ إِلَّاتَجِدُهُ مَلْآنَ ذَهَبٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kulla mā jāʾa ka al-mawāshiṭu wa-al-maghānī wa-al-dāyātu ḥuṭṭa yadaka fī jaybika tajidhu malʾāna dhahabin fa-ukmush wa-irmi lahum wa-lā-tatawahham annaka lā-tudkhilu yadaka illā-tajiduhu malʾāna dhahabin
sentences.l: And every-time came you the-hairdressers and-the-singing-women and-the-nurses, put your-hand in your-pocket, you-find-it full-of gold; then-grab and-throw to-them. And-do-not imagine that-you not you-put-in your-hand except you-find-it full-of gold.
sentences.i: Whenever the dressers and the singing-women and the nurses come to you, put your hand in your pocket and you will find it full of gold; grab a handful and throw it to them. And do not imagine that you will ever put in your hand without finding it full of gold.
sentences.n: In the print ك is a separate word: جَاءَ كَ is جَاءَكَ, "came to you". The ladies who come to be tipped are the المواشط (the women who dress and adorn a bride), the singing-women, and the الدايات (nurses, midwives). مَلْآنَ ذَهَبٍ, literally "full of gold", puts the material in the genitive; Classical would have an accusative. In وَلَاتَتَوَهَّمْ the لا is printed joined to the verb, as in لَاتُدْخِلُ.

sentences.t: فَنَقِّطْ كُلَّ مَنْ أَتَى إِلَيْكَ بِالْحَفْنَةِ وَلَا تَخْشَ مِنْ شَيْ
sentences.tr: fa-naqqiṭ kulla man atā ilayka bi-al-ḥafnati wa-lā takhsha min shay
sentences.l: So-tip every one-who came to-you, with-the-handful; and-do-not fear of anything.
sentences.i: Tip everyone who comes to you with a handful, and fear nothing.
sentences.n: نَقِّطْ is the Egyptian-flavoured verb for scattering coins as a gift to performers (نُقْطَة). شَيْ is the print's spelling of شَيْء, "thing"; it is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَمَا هَذَا بِحَوْلِكَ بَلْ هَذَا بِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-tawakkal ʿalā alladhī khalaqaka fa-mā hādhā bi-ḥawlika bal hādhā bi-amri Allāhi
sentences.l: And-put-your-trust upon the-one-who created-you; for-not this is by-your-power, rather this is by-the-command of-God.
sentences.i: And put your trust in the One who created you: this is not by your own power, but by God's command.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ مِنَ الْعِفْرِيتِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ قَالَ يَا تُرَٰي أَيْشْ تَكُونُ هَذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةُ وَمَا سَبَبُ الْإِحْسَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa badru al-dīni ḥasanun min al-ʿifrīti hādhā al-kalāma qāla yā turā ayshi takūnu hādhihi al-ṣabiyyatu wa-mā sababu al-iḥsāni
sentences.l: And-when heard Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan from the-ifrit this the-speech, he-said: O I-wonder, what-thing she-is this the-girl, and-what the-cause of-the-benefaction?
sentences.i: When Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan heard these words from the ifrit, he said, "I wonder who this girl may be, and what is the reason for this kindness?"
sentences.n: يَا تُرَى (printed تري) is a colloquial "I wonder"; ايش is the colloquial "what?" (أَيُّ شَيْءٍ). The name بدرالدين is printed as one word and is pointed in one piece.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَشَى وَأَوْقَدَ الشَّمْعَةَ وَجَاءَ إِلَى الْحَمَّامِ فَوَجَدَ الْأَحْدَبَ رَاكِبَ الْفَرَسِ فَدَخَلَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَهُوَ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ وَالصُّورَةِ الْحَسَنَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma mashā wa-awqada al-shamʿata wa-jāʾa ilā al-ḥammāmi fa-wajada al-aḥdaba rākiba al-farasi fa-dakhala badru al-dīni ḥasanun bayna al-nāsi wa-huwa ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati wa-al-ṣūrati al-ḥasanati
sentences.l: Then he-walked and-lit the-candle and-came to the-bath-house and-found the-hunchback riding-of the-horse; and-entered Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan among the-people, and-he upon that the-state and-the-form the-beautiful.
sentences.i: Then he set out, lit the candle, and came to the bathhouse, where he found the hunchback mounted on his horse. Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan went in among the crowd, in that same state and in that same handsome figure.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ عَلَيْهِ كَمَا ذَكَرْنَا الطَّرْبُوشُ وَالشَّاشُ وَالْفَرَجِيَّةُ الْمَنْسُوجَةُ بِالذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ʿalayhi kamā dhakarnā al-ṭarbūshu wa-al-shāshu wa-al-farajiyyatu al-mansūjatu bi-al-dhahabi
sentences.l: And-was upon-him, as we-mentioned, the-tarbush and-the-shash and-the-farajiyya the-woven with-the-gold.
sentences.i: And upon him, as we have told, were the tarbush, the muslin turban-cloth, and the long robe woven with gold.
sentences.n: الطربوش is the fez, الشاش the muslin wound around it as a turban, and الفرجية a long, wide-sleeved outer robe. "As we mentioned" is the narrator pointing back to the earlier description of his dress.

sentences.t: وَمَازَالَ مَاشِيًا فِى الزِّينَةِ وَكُلَّمَا وَقَفَتِ الْمَغَانِي وَالنَّاسُ يُنَقِّطُ وَيَحُطُّ يَدَهُ فِي جَيْبِهِ يَلْقَاهُ مَلْآنَ ذَهَبٍ فَيَكْمُشُ وَيَرْمِي فِى الطَّارِ الَّذِي فِى الْمُغَنِّيَةِ فَيَمْلَأُ الطَّارَ دَنَانِيرَ
sentences.tr: wa-māzāla māshiyan fī al-zīnati wa-kullamā waqafati al-maghānī wa-al-nāsu yunaqqiṭu wa-yaḥuṭṭu yadahu fī jaybihi yalqāhu malʾāna dhahabin fa-yakmushu wa-yarmī fī al-ṭāri alladhī fī al-mughanniyati fa-yamlaʾu al-ṭāra danānīra
sentences.l: And-he-ceased-not walking in the-adornment; and-every-time stopped the-singing-women, and-the-people, he-tips and-puts his-hand in his-pocket, he-finds-it full-of gold; so-he-grabs and-throws into the-tambourine which is in the-singing-woman, and-fills the-tambourine dinars.
sentences.i: And he went on walking in the wedding train; and whenever the singing-women halted, with the people about them, he would tip them: he put his hand in his pocket and found it full of gold, took up a handful and threw it into the tambourine the singing-woman held, and so filled the tambourine with dinars.
sentences.n: والناس ينقط is loose in the print: "the people" is a stray subject for a verb whose real subject is Badr al-Dīn (singular يُنَقِّطُ). الزينة is the "adornment", the festive display of the wedding procession. الطار is the frame-drum or tambourine, and في المغنية, "in the singing-woman", means in her hand.

sentences.t: فَاخْتَرَعَتْ عُقُولُ الْمَغَانِي وَتَعَجَّبَ النَّاسُ مِنْ حُسْنِهِ وَجَمَالِهِ وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا لِبَيْتِ الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-ikhtaraʿat ʿuqūlu al-maghānī wa-taʿajjaba al-nāsu min ḥusnihi wa-jamālihi wa-lam yazālū ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli ḥattā waṣalū li-bayti al-wazīri
sentences.l: And-originated (so printed) the-minds of-the-singing-women, and-marvelled the-people at his-beauty and-his-comeliness; and-not they-ceased upon this the-state until they-arrived at-the-house of-the-vizier.
sentences.i: The singing-women's wits were carried clean away, and the people marvelled at his beauty and comeliness; and so they went on until they reached the vizier's house.
sentences.n: فَاخْتَرَعَتْ عُقُولُ is obscure: اِخْتَرَعَ is "to originate, invent", which does not suit "minds". The print may be corrupt for something like اِخْتَلَبَتْ "were charmed, bewitched"; the idiomatic line follows that guess. لِبَيْتِ is لِـ of motion, "to", where Classical would use إلى.

sentences.t: فَرَدَّتِ الْحُجَّابُ النَّاسَ وَمَنَعُوهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-raddati al-ḥujjābu al-nāsa wa-manaʿūhum
sentences.l: And-turned-back the-doorkeepers the-people and-prevented-them.
sentences.i: But the chamberlains turned the people back and held them off.
sentences.n: الحجاب are the chamberlains or doorkeepers. The verb is feminine singular, the regular agreement with a plural of things or groups, and then switches to the masculine plural (وَمَنَعُوهُمْ).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْمَغَانِي وَاللَّهِ لَا يَدْخُلُ إِلَّا أَنْ دَخَلَ هَذَا الشَّابُّ مَعَنَا لِأَنَّهُ عَمَّرَنَا بِإِحْسَانِهِ وَلَا نَجْلِي الْعَرُوسَةَ إِلَّا وَهُوَ حَاضِرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-maghānī wa-Allāhi lā yadkhulu illā an dakhala hādhā al-shābbu maʿanā li-annahu ʿammaranā bi-iḥsānihi wa-lā najlī al-ʿarūsata illā wa-huwa ḥāḍirun
sentences.l: And-said the-singing-women: By-God, not he-enters except that entered this the-youth with-us, because-he made-us-flourish with-his-bounty; and-not we-unveil the-bride except while-he present.
sentences.i: Then the singing-women said, "By God, no one shall go in unless this young man goes in with us: he has made us rich with his bounty, and we will not display the bride unless he is present."
sentences.n: إِلَّا أَنْ دَخَلَ has the perfect after "unless", where Classical would have a subjunctive: "unless (it be that) he has entered". جَلَا الْعَرُوسَةَ is the technical phrase for unveiling and displaying the bride to the guests.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ دَخَلُوا بِهِ إِلَى قَاعَةِ الْفَرَحِ وَأَجْلَسُوهُ فَوْقَ عَيْنِ الْعَرِيسِ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika dakhalū bihi ilā qāʿati al-faraḥi wa-ajlasūhu fawqa ʿayni al-ʿarīsi al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: And-at that they-entered with-him to the-hall of-the-joy and-seated-him above the-eye of-the-bridegroom the-hunchback.
sentences.i: Thereupon they took him into the wedding hall and seated him above the hunchbacked bridegroom, on his right.
sentences.n: The print has عين, "eye", where the ifrit's instruction said "above the right (يمين) of the bridegroom". It is probably a slip for يَمِين; عَيْن can also mean "the choice part, the person", so a sense of "in the place of honour" is possible. قاعة الفرح is the wedding hall.

sentences.t: وَاصْطَفَّتْ جَمِيعُ نِسَاءِ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْوُزَرَاءِ وَالْحُجَّابِ صَفَّيْنِ وَكُلُّ امْرَأَةٍ مَعَهَا شَمْعَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ مَوْقُودَةٌ ضَارِبَةَ لِثَامٍ وَهُنَّ صُفُوفٌ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا مِنْ تَحْتِ الْمِنَصَّةِ إِلَى صَدْرِ الْإِيوَانِ الَّذِي عِنْدَ الْمَجْلِسِ الَّذِي تَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْعَرُوسَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-iṣṭaffat jamīʿu nisāʾi al-umarāʾi wa-al-wuzarāʾi wa-al-ḥujjābi ṣaffayni wa-kullu imraʾatin maʿahā shamʿatun kabīratun mawqūdatun ḍāribata lithāmin wa-hunna ṣufūfun yamīnan wa-shimālan min taḥti al-minaṣṣati ilā ṣadri al-īwāni alladhī ʿinda al-majlisi alladhī takhruju minhu al-ʿarūsatu
sentences.l: And-lined-up all women-of the-emirs and-the-viziers and-the-chamberlains, two-rows; and-every woman with-her a-candle large lit, veil-striking; and-they rows right and-left, from beneath the-dais to the-top-of the-īwān which is at the-seat which comes-out from-it the-bride.
sentences.i: And all the wives of the emirs, viziers and chamberlains drew up in two rows, each woman with a tall lit candle, veiled; and they stood in ranks to right and left, from the foot of the dais to the head of the īwān, where the seat is from which the bride comes out.
sentences.n: ضَارِبَةَ لِثَامٍ, literally "striking a veil", means having drawn a face-veil on. المنصة is the dais on which the bride is displayed; الايوان is the īwān, the vaulted hall open on one side. In the print صفين is the dual, "two rows", then صفوف, "ranks".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتِ النِّسَاءُ بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ وَمَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحُسْنِ وَالْجَمَالِ وَوَجْهُهُ يُضِيءُ كَأَنَّهُ الْهِلَالُ فَمِلْنَ جَمِيعُ النِّسَاءِ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarati al-nisāʾu badra al-dīni ḥasana wa-mā ʿalayhi min al-ḥusni wa-al-jamāli wa-wajhuhu yuḍīʾu ka-annahu al-hilālu fa-milna jamīʿu al-nisāʾi ilayhi
sentences.l: And-when looked the-women [at] Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan and-what is-upon-him of the-beauty and-the-comeliness, and-his-face shining as-if-it the-crescent, they-inclined, all the-women, to-him.
sentences.i: When the women looked at Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and saw all the beauty and comeliness that was on him, and his face shining like the new moon, they all inclined toward him.
sentences.n: حَسَنَ is pointed with a bare fatḥa: as an accusative the name would take -an, which needs an alif the print does not have.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْمَغَانِي لِلنِّسَاءِ الْحَاضِرَاتِ اعْلَمْنَ أَنَّ هَذَا الْمَلِيحَ مَانَقَّطَنَا إِلَّا بِالذَّهَبِ الْأَحْمَرِ فَلَا تُقَصِّرْنَ فِي خِدْمَتِهِ وَأَطِعْنَهُ فِيمَا يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-maghānī li-al-nisāʾi al-ḥāḍirāti iʿlamna anna hādhā al-malīḥa mā-naqqaṭanā illā bi-al-dhahabi al-aḥmari fa-lā tuqaṣṣirna fī khidmatihi wa-aṭiʿnahu fīmā yaqūlu
sentences.l: And-said the-singing-women to-the-women the-present: Know that this the-fair-one not-he-tipped-us except with-the-gold the-red; so-do-not fall-short in his-service, and-obey-him in-what he-says.
sentences.i: And the singing-women said to the women present, "Know that this handsome youth has tipped us with nothing but red gold, so do not fall short in serving him, and obey him in whatever he says."
sentences.n: المليح, "the fair one", is the usual word for a good-looking youth. مَانَقَّطَنَا is printed as one word, ما نقطنا.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَازْدَحَمَتِ النِّسَاءُ عَلَيْهِ بِالشَّمْعِ وَ نَظَرْنَ إِلَى جَمَالِهِ وَحَسَدْنَهُ عَلَٰي حُسْنِهِ وَصَارَتْ كُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ تَوَدُّأَنْ تَكُونَ فِي حِضْنِهِ سَاعَةً أَوْ سَنَةً
sentences.tr: qāla fa-izdaḥamati al-nisāʾu ʿalayhi bi-al-shamʿi wa nazarna ilā jamālihi wa-ḥasadnahu ʿalā ḥusnihi wa-ṣārat kullu wāḥidatin minhunna tawaddu-an takūna fī ḥiḍnihi sāʿatan aw sanatan
sentences.l: He-said: And-crowded the-women upon-him with-the-candles, and they-looked to his-comeliness, and-envied-him upon his-beauty; and-became every one of-them wishing that she-be in his-lap an-hour or a-year.
sentences.i: He said: The women crowded round him with their candles, gazed at his comeliness, and envied him his beauty; and every one of them longed to be in his arms for an hour, or a year.
sentences.n: The lone و before نظرن is how the print has it, apparently a line-end split of وَنَظَرْنَ; the pointing keeps it as a separate word. تَوَدُّا^َنْ is تَوَدُّ أَنْ, "she wishes to", run together. قال is the narrator's "he said", the chain of reporters.

sentences.t: فَأَرْخَيْنَ مَاكَانَ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِنَّ لَمَّا غَابَ عَنْهُنَّ الْأَلْبَابُ وَقُلْنَ هَنِيأً لِمَنْ كَانَ لَهُ أَوْ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ الشَّابُّ
sentences.tr: fa-arkhayna mā-kāna ʿalā wujūhihinna lammā ghāba ʿanhunna al-albābu wa-qulna hanīʾan li-man kāna lahu aw ʿalayhi dhālika al-shābbu
sentences.l: And-they-let-down what-was upon their-faces when departed from-them the-minds; and-they-said: Wholesome! for-whom was for-him or against-him that the-youth.
sentences.i: They let fall what was over their faces, for their wits had left them, and they said, "Happy the woman who has that youth, whether he be for her or against her!"
sentences.n: ما كان على وجوههن is the veils drawn over their faces (لِثَام, above). لَهُ أَوْ عَلَيْهِ, "for him or against him", is a set phrase meaning "for better or worse"; the print's wording is compressed and the sense given is a best reading. هنيأ is printed with a hamza on the alif-less seat and is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَعَوْنَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ السَّائِسِ الْأَحْدَبِ وَمَنْ كَانَ لَهُ سَبَبًا فِي زَوَاجِهِ هَذِهِ الْمَلِيحَةَ وَصِرْنَ كُلَّمَا دَعَوْنَ لِبَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ دَعَوْنَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: thumma daʿawna ʿalā dhālika al-sāʾisi al-aḥdabi wa-man kāna lahu sababan fī zawājihi hādhihi al-malīḥata wa-ṣirna kullamā daʿawna li-badri al-dīni ḥasanin daʿawna ʿalā dhālika al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: Then they-invoked upon that the-groom the-hunchback and-whoever was for-him a-cause in his-marrying this the-fair-one; and-they-became, every-time they-invoked for Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan, they-invoked upon that the-hunchback.
sentences.i: Then they called down curses upon that hunchbacked groom, and on anyone who had had a hand in his marrying this fair girl; and every time they prayed for Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, they prayed against that hunchback.
sentences.n: دَعَا لِـ is "pray for" and دَعَا عَلَى "pray against, curse". زَوَاجِهِ هَذِهِ الْمَلِيحَةَ is "his marrying this fair one": the noun takes its object directly.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَغَانِيَ ضَرَبْنَ بِالدُّفُوفِ وَزَعَقْنَ بِالْمَوَاصِلِ وَأَقْبَلَتِ الْمَوَاشِطُ وَبِنْتُ الْوَزِيرِ بَيْنَهُنَّ وَقَدْ طَيَّبُوهَا وَعَطَّرُوهَا وَحَسَّنُوا شَعْرَهَا وَبَخَّرُوهَا وَأَلْبَسُوهَا الْحُلِيَّ وَالْحُلَلَ مِنْ لِبَاسِ الْمُلُوكِ الْأَكَاسِرَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-maghāniya ḍarabna bi-al-dufūfi wa-zaʿaqna bi-al-mawāṣili wa-aqbalati al-mawāshiṭu wa-bintu al-wazīri baynahunna wa-qad ṭayyabūhā wa-ʿaṭṭarūhā wa-ḥassanū shaʿrahā wa-bakhkharūhā wa-albasūhā al-ḥuliyya wa-al-ḥulala min libāsi al-mulūki al-akāsirati
sentences.l: Then indeed the-singing-women struck with-the-tambourines and-cried-out with-the-mawāṣil; and-came-forward the-hairdressers, and-the-daughter of-the-vizier among-them, and-they-had perfumed-her and-scented-her and-beautified her-hair and-fumigated-her and-clothed-her the-jewellery and-the-robes from the-clothing of-the-kings the-Chosroes.
sentences.i: Then the singing-women beat their tambourines and raised the mawāṣil, and the dressers came forward with the vizier's daughter among them, having perfumed and scented her, dressed her hair, fumigated her with incense, and clothed her in the jewels and robes of the Chosroes, the kings of Persia.
sentences.n: المواصل is obscure: it may be strains or songs "joined" together, but I cannot name the exact musical term, so it is left in transliteration. زَعَقَ is to cry out shrilly. بخروها is to perfume with incense (بَخُور). الأكاسرة are the Khosrows, the Sasanian kings, used for "kings of old". بالدفوف, "with the tambourines", has بِـ marking the instrument struck.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ جُمْلَةِ مَا عَلَيْهَا ثَوْبٌ مَنْقُوشٌ بِالذَّهَبِ الْأَحْمَرِ فِيهِ صُوَرُ الْوُحُوشِ وَالطُّيُورِ وَهُوَ مَسْبُولٌ عَلَيْهَا مِنْ فَوْقِ حَوَائِجِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-min jumlati mā ʿalayhā thawbun manqūshun bi-al-dhahabi al-aḥmari fīhi ṣuwaru al-wuḥūshi wa-al-ṭuyūri wa-huwa masbūlun ʿalayhā min fawqi ḥawāʾijihā
sentences.l: And-from the-totality-of what is-upon-her, a-garment embroidered with-the-gold the-red, in-it images-of the-wild-beasts and-the-birds, and-it let-down upon-her from above her-garments.
sentences.i: Among all that she wore was a robe embroidered in red gold, with figures of beasts and birds, and it hung loose upon her, over her other garments.
sentences.n: الحوائج is the plural of حَاجَة, "need" or "thing needed", used here for her clothes and gear.

sentences.t: وَقَلَّدُوهَا بِعِقْدٍ يَمَنِيٍّ يُسَاوِى الْأُلُوفَ وَقَدْ حَوَى كُلَّ فَصِّ جَوْهَرٍ مَاحَازَ مِثْلَهُ تُبَّعٌ وَلَا قَيْصَرُ
sentences.tr: wa-qalladūhā bi-ʿiqdin yamaniyyin yusāwī al-ulūfa wa-qad ḥawā kulla faṣṣi jawharin mā-ḥāza mithlahu tubbaʿun wa-lā qayṣaru
sentences.l: And-they-collared-her with-a-necklace Yemeni, it-equals the-thousands, and-it-had contained every stone-of jewel which-not possessed the-like-of-it Tubbaʿ nor Caesar.
sentences.i: And they hung about her neck a Yemeni necklace worth thousands, which held in every setting a jewel the like of which neither Tubbaʿ nor Caesar ever possessed.
sentences.n: قَلَّدَ بِـ is "to put a necklace (by means of ...) on someone". تُبَّع is the title of the ancient South Arabian kings, here and قَيْصَر standing for the richest rulers of East and West. يُسَاوِى keeps the print's final ى and is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: وَالْعَرُوسَةُ كَأَنَّهَا الْبَدْرُ إِذَا بَدَا فِى اللَّيْلَةِ أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ʿarūsatu ka-annahā al-badru idhā badā fī al-laylati arbaʿata ʿashara
sentences.l: And-the-bride as-if-she the-full-moon when it-appeared in the-night fourteen.
sentences.i: And the bride was like the full moon when it shows on the fourteenth night.
sentences.n: The full moon is the moon of the fourteenth night of the month. The print has the definite الليلة before the number ("the night fourteen").

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَتْ كَانَتْ كَأَنَّهَا حُورِيَّةٌ فَسُبْحَانَ مَنْ خَلَقَهَا بَهِيَّةً
sentences.tr: wa-lammā aqbalat kānat ka-annahā ḥūriyyatun fa-subḥāna man khalaqahā bahiyyatan
sentences.l: And-when she-approached she-was as-if-she a-houri; and-glory to-the-one-who created-her radiant.
sentences.i: And when she came forward she was like a houri of Paradise: glory to Him who created her so radiant!

sentences.t: وَأَحْدَقُوا بِهَا النِّسَاءُ فَصِرْنَ كَالنُّجُومِ وَهُوَ بَيْنَهُنَّ كَلْقَمَرِ إِذَا انْجَلَا عِنْدَالْغَيْمِ
sentences.tr: wa-aḥdaqū bihā al-nisāʾu fa-ṣirna ka-al-nujūmi wa-huwa baynahunna ka-al-qamari idhā injalā ʿinda al-ghaymi
sentences.l: And-surrounded her the-women, and-they-became like-the-stars, and-he among-them like-the-moon when it-cleared at the-cloud.
sentences.i: The women crowded round her and became like the stars, and she among them like the moon when it breaks clear of the clouds.
sentences.n: The print has masculine وَهُوَ, "and he", but the comparison fits the bride (وَهِيَ); the idiomatic line follows the sense. كلقمر is printed without the alif of the article and is pointed كَلْقَمَرِ, ka-al-qamar; عندالغيم is likewise one word, عِنْدَ الْغَيْمِ, "at the clouds", i.e. out from among them. وَأَحْدَقُوا ... النِّسَاءُ has a plural verb before its subject.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ الْبَصْرِيُّ جَالِسًا وَالنَّاسُ نَاظِرُونَ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna badru al-dīni ḥasanun al-baṣriyyu jāliṣan wa-al-nāsu nāẓirūna ilayhi
sentences.l: And-was Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan the-Baṣran sitting, and-the-people looking to-him.
sentences.i: And Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan of Basra sat there, with the people looking at him.

sentences.t: فَخَطَرَتِ الْعَرُوسَةُ وَأَقْبَلَتْ وَتَمَايَلَتْ فَقَامَ إِلَيْهَا السَّائِسُ الْأَحْدَبُ لِيُقَبِّلَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-khaṭarati al-ʿarūsatu wa-aqbalat wa-tamāyalat fa-qāma ilayhā al-sāʾisu al-aḥdabu li-yuqabbilahā
sentences.l: And-strutted the-bride, and-came-forward, and-swayed; and-rose to-her the-groom the-hunchback, in-order-that-he-kiss-her.
sentences.i: The bride paced forward, swaying, and the hunchbacked groom rose and went to her to kiss her.

sentences.t: فَأَعْرَضَتْ عَنْهُ وَانْفَتَلَتْ حَتَّى صَارَتْ قُدَّامَ حَسَنِ بْنِ عَمِّهَا فَضَحِكَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿraḍat ʿanhu wa-infatalat ḥattā ṣārat quddāma ḥasani bni ʿammihā fa-ḍaḥikat
sentences.l: And-she-turned-away from-him and-twisted-round until she-came-to-be before Ḥasan, son-of her-uncle, and-she-laughed.
sentences.i: She turned away from him and twisted round until she stood before Ḥasan, her cousin, and she laughed.
sentences.n: ابن عمها, 'son of her paternal uncle', is how Arabic says 'male cousin'; this is Ḥasan Badr al-Dīn, whom the bride is really to marry.

sentences.t: النَّاسُ فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا مَالَتْ إِلَى نَحْوَحَسَنٍ بَدْرِالدِّينِ ضَجَّتِ النَّاسُ وَصَرَخَتِ الْمَغَانِي
sentences.tr: al-nāsu fa-lammā raʾawhā mālat ilā naḥwaḥasanin badri al-dīni ḍajjati al-nāsu wa-ṣarakhati al-maghānī
sentences.l: The-people — and-when they-saw-her (that) she-inclined toward-Ḥasan Badr-al-Dīn, the-people cried-out, and-shrieked the-singing-women.
sentences.i: And when the people saw her incline toward Ḥasan Badr al-Dīn, they cried out, and the singing-women shrieked.
sentences.n: The first الناس is left hanging and picked up again by the second, a spoken-style repetition. Both verbs are feminine singular with plural-sense subjects, normal for a collective and common in Middle Arabic. المغاني is the hired singing-women of a wedding; the form is obscure to me (perhaps a plural of غانية or of مغنية), and the sense is certain from the context.

sentences.t: فَحَطَّ يَدَهُ فِي جَيْبِهِ وَكَمَشَ وَرَمَى فِي طِيرَانِ الْمَغَانِي فَفَرِحُوا
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaṭṭa yadahu fī jaybihi wa-kamasha wa-ramā fī ṭīrāni al-maghānī fa-fariḥū
sentences.l: And-he-put his-hand into his-pocket and-grabbed-a-handful and-threw into the-tambourines-of the-singing-women, and-they-rejoiced.
sentences.i: He put his hand into his pocket, took out a handful, and threw it into the singing-women's tambourines, and they rejoiced.
sentences.n: The print does not say what he threw; it can only be coin, since throwing money to the singing-women is a wedding custom. I read طيران as the plural of طار, 'tambourine'; the word could be read otherwise, and I note it as a reading, not a certainty.

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا كُنَّا نَشْتَهِي أَنْ تَكُونَ هَذِهِ الْعَرُوسَةُ لَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālū kunnā nashtahī an takūna hādhihi al-ʿarūsatu laka
sentences.l: And-they-said: We-were desiring that-she-be this bride for-you.
sentences.i: And they said, "We had been wishing that this bride might be yours."

sentences.t: فَتَبَسَّمَ هَذَا كُلُّهُمْ أَحْدَ قُوا بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-tabassama hādhā kulluhum aḥda qū bihi
sentences.l: And-he-smiled, this-one; all-of-them [aḥdaqū] surrounded him.
sentences.i: And this one smiled, and they all crowded around him.
sentences.n: The print has no stop here, and it breaks أحدقوا into أحد قوا. I read هذا as Ḥasan, 'this one', who smiles at the singing-women's praise while the guests throng him.

sentences.t: وَبَقِيَ السَّائِسُ الْأَحْدَبُ وَحْدَةُ كَأَنَّهُ قِرْدُو كُلَّمَا أَوْ قَدُوا لَهُ الشَّمْعَةَ فَلَا يَقْدِرُ وَلَا بَقِيَ لَهُ صَوْتٌ وَصَارَ قَاعِدًا فِي الظَّلَامِ وَيَنْظُرُ فِى نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-baqiya al-sāʾisu al-aḥdabu waḥdahu ka-annahu qirdū kullamā aw qaduwā lahu al-shamʿata fa-lā yaqdiru wa-lā baqiya lahu ṣawtun wa-ṣāra qāʿidan fī al-ẓalāmi wa-yanẓuru fī nafsihi
sentences.l: And-there-remained the-groom, the-hunchback, alone, as-if-he (were) an-ape; whenever they-lit for-him the-candle, he-is-not-able, and-no voice remained to-him, and-he-came-to-be sitting in the-darkness, and-he-looks into his-self.
sentences.i: And the hunchbacked groom was left alone, like an ape; whenever they lit the candle for him he was helpless, and no voice was left to him; he sat in the darkness and looked into himself.
sentences.n: Two words are split by the print, أو قدوا for أوقدوا. The print does not say what he cannot do with the candle (hold it, bear it); I leave the verb without a complement, as it is. نظر في نفسه, 'look into oneself', means to consider, reflect. وحدة ends in ة where the pronoun ه is meant, as in a few more words below; I point the ة as if it were ه.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ فَإِنَّهُ صَارَ قُدَّامَهُ شُمُوعٌ فِي أَيْدِي النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā badru al-dīni ḥasanun fa-innahu ṣāra quddāmahu shumūʿun fī aydī al-nāsi
sentences.l: And-as-for Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan, then-he — came-to-be before-him candles in the-hands-of the-people.
sentences.i: As for Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, there were candles before him, in the people's hands.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ حَسَنٌ إِلَى الْعَرِيسِ وَحْدَةُ فِى الظَّلَامِ وَنَظَرَ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ النَّاسَ مُحْدِقِينَ بِهِ وَهَذِةِ الشُّمُوعَ الْمُوقَدَةَ تَحَيَّرَ وَتَعَجَّبَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara ḥasanun ilā al-ʿarīsi waḥdahu fī al-ẓalāmi wa-naẓara fī nafsihi wa-hāʾulāʾi al-nāsa muḥdiqīna bihi wa-hādhihi al-shumūʿa al-mūqadata taḥayyara wa-taʿajjaba
sentences.l: And-when Ḥasan looked at the-bridegroom, alone in the-darkness, and-looked in himself, and these the-people surrounding him, and these the-candles, the-lit — he-was-bewildered and-marvelled.
sentences.i: And when Ḥasan looked at the bridegroom, alone in the darkness, and considered, and saw these people thronging around him and these lighted candles, he was bewildered and marvelled.
sentences.n: The sentence piles up what Ḥasan sees and only reaches its verb, تحير وتعجب, at the end. I point the people and the candles as objects of 'looked' to make that work. هذة is printed for هذه.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ ابْنَتَ عَمِّهِ فَرِحَ وَاسْتَبْشَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā badru al-dīni ḥasanun ibnata ʿammihi fariḥa wa-istabshara
sentences.l: And-when he-saw Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan the-daughter-of his-uncle, he-rejoiced and-took-glad-heart.
sentences.i: And when Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan saw his cousin, he rejoiced and was glad.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ نَظَرَ إِلَى وَجْهِهَا وَقَدْأَ شْرَقَ بِالنُّورِ وَأَزْهَرَ لَاسِيَّمَا وَعَلَيْهَا تِلْكَ الْبَدْلَةُ الْأَطْلَسُ الْأَحْمَرُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad naẓara ilā wajhihā wa-qada shraqa bi-al-nūri wa-azhara lāsiyyamā wa-ʿalayhā tilka al-badlatu al-aṭlasu al-aḥmaru
sentences.l: And-he-had looked at her-face, and-(it) had shone with-the-light and-bloomed, especially (as) upon-her (was) that the-suit, the-satin, the-red.
sentences.i: He had looked at her face, and it shone with light and bloomed — all the more because she wore that red satin suit.
sentences.n: The print writes وقدا شرق, putting the alif of أشرق on the wrong word; I keep the split. Her face is the subject of 'shone' and 'bloomed'. الاطلس, 'the satin', stands beside البدلة as an apposition.

sentences.t: فَجَلَوْهَا الْمَوَاشِطُ أَوَّلَ خِلْعَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-jalawhā al-mawāshiṭu awwala khilʿatin
sentences.l: And-they-displayed-her, the-dressers, a-first robe.
sentences.i: And the dressers displayed her in the first robe.
sentences.n: The plural verb comes before its plural subject (جلوها المواشط, 'they displayed her, the dressers'), which is ordinary in Middle Arabic. جلا العروس is the idiom for showing off the bride in her successive dresses.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَ حُسْنُ الطَّلْعَةِ فَتَعَاجَبَتْ وَتَمَايَلَتْ مِنَ الدَّلَالِ وَأَذْهَاتْ عُقُولَ النِّسَاءِ وَالرِّجَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadha ḥusnu al-ṭalʿati fa-taʿājabat wa-tamāyalat mina al-dalāli wa-adhhāt ʿuqūla al-nisāʾi wa-al-rijāli
sentences.l: And-took the-beauty-of the-aspect; so-she-preened and-swayed out-of the-coquetry, and-bewildered [adhhāt] the-minds-of the-women and-the-men.
sentences.i: Her beauty took hold; she preened and swayed in her coquetry, and dazzled the wits of women and men alike.
sentences.n: This is the obscure place of the passage. As printed, واخذ حسن الطلعة has no object; I read حُسْنُ الطَّلْعَةِ, 'the beauty of her aspect', as the subject of أخذ, 'took hold' (of the onlookers). A reader who sees حسن as the name Ḥasan would read it as 'and Ḥasan took in the sight'; the print cannot decide between them. اذهات is printed for اذهلت, 'she bewildered'; the letter ل has become an alif.

sentences.t: فَكَانَتْ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا الشَّاعِرُ الْمِفْضَالُ شِـــــــعْـــــــرًا
sentences.tr: fa-kānat ka-mā qāla fīhā al-shāʿiru al-mifḍālu shiʿran
sentences.l: And-she-was as said about-her the-poet, the-bountiful, in-verse:
sentences.i: And she was just as the gracious poet has said of her, in verse:

sentences.t:
وَشَمْسٍ فِي قَضِيبٍ فِي كَثِيبٍ * تَبَدَّتْ فِي قَمِيصٍ جُلَّنَارِ
سَقَتْنِي رِيقَ خَمْرَتِهَا وَجَادَتْ * بِوَجْنَتِهَا فَاطْفَتْ جُلَّ نَارِ
sentences.tr:
wa-shamsin fī qaḍībin fī kathībin * tabaddat fī qamīṣin julnāri
saqatnī rīqa khamratihā wa-jādat * bi-wajnatihā fa-aṭfat julla nāri
sentences.l:
And a-sun in a-branch in a-dune, * she-appeared in a-shirt of-pomegranate-blossom;
She-gave-me-to-drink the-saliva-of her-wine and-was-generous * with-her-cheek, and-so-put-out most-of a-fire.
sentences.i: A sun upon a slender bough upon a dune of sand: she appeared in a shift the colour of pomegranate blossom. She gave me to drink the spittle of her wine, and was bountiful with her cheek, and so put out the greater part of a fire.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse and the pointing is kept as printed. The rhyme-words جُلَّنَارِ, 'pomegranate blossom', and جُلَّ نَارِ, 'most of a fire', are the same letters with different meanings, a pun English cannot keep; the fire is the lover's passion, put out by her cheek's kisses. The print gives فَاطْفَتْ for فَأَطْفَأَتْ, without the hamza.

sentences.t: وَغَيَّرُوا تِلْكَ الْبَدْلَةَ وَأَلْبَسُوهَا ثَوْبًا أَزْرَقَ فَطَلَعَتْ كَالْبَدْرِ إِذَا أَشْرَقَ ذَاتَ شَعْرٍ فَاحِمٍ وَخَدٍّنَا عِمٍ وَثَغْرٍ بَاسِمٍ وَنَهْدٍ قَائِمٍ وَهِيَ رَابِيَةُ الْأَطْرٰفِ وَالْمَعَاصِمِ
sentences.tr: wa-ghayyarū tilka al-badlata wa-albasūhā thawban azraqa fa-ṭalaʿat ka-al-badri idhā ashraqa dhāta shaʿrin fāḥimin wa-khaddin nā ʿimin wa-thaghrin bāsimin wa-nahdin qāʾimin wa-hiya rābiyatu al-aṭrāfi wa-al-maʿāṣimi
sentences.l: And-they-changed that the-suit and-clothed-her a-garment blue, and-she-came-forth like-the-full-moon when it-shines, possessor-of hair jet-black, and-a-cheek [nā]-soft, and-a-mouth smiling, and-a-breast firm, and-she (was) swelling-of the-extremities and-the-wrists.
sentences.i: They changed that outfit and dressed her in a blue gown, and she came forth like the full moon when it shines, with jet-black hair, a soft cheek, a smiling mouth and a firm breast, plump of limb and wrist.
sentences.n: The print splits ناعم into وخدنا عم; I keep the split. الاطرف lacks the alif of الأطراف; it is restored with the dagger alif. The run of descriptions after ذات is the typical Nights portrait of a bride, each with its own genitive, 'having hair ..., a cheek ...'.

sentences.t: وَجَلَوْهَا الْخِلْعَهَ الثَّانِيَةَ وَكَانَتْ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا أَصْحَابُ الْهِمَمِ الْعَالِيَةِ شِـــــــعْـــــــرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-jalawhā al-khilʿaha al-thāniyata wa-kānat ka-mā qāla fīhā aṣḥābu al-himami al-ʿāliyati shiʿrun
sentences.l: And-they-displayed-her the-robe the-second, and-she-was as said about-her the-possessors-of the-aspirations, the-lofty, verse:
sentences.i: They displayed her in the second robe, and she was as the men of lofty aspirations have said of her, in verse:
sentences.n: The print writes the ending of الخلعة sometimes with ة and sometimes with ه (الخلعه); both are read -a. أصحاب الهمم العالية, 'men of lofty aspirations', is a grand way of saying 'poets'.

sentences.t:
اَقْبَلَتْ فِي غُلَالَةٍ زُرْقَةٍ * لَازَوَرْدِيَّةٍ كَلَوْنِ السَّمَاءِ
فَتَامَّلْتُ فِي الْغَلَالَةِ مِنْهَا * قَمَرُ الصَّيْفِ فِي لَيَالِي الشِّتَاءِ
sentences.tr:
aqbalat fī ghulālatin zurqatin * lāzawardiyyatin ka-lawni al-samāʾi
fa-tāmmaltu fī al-ghalālati minhā * qamaru al-ṣayfi fī layālī al-shitāʾi
sentences.l:
She-came-on in a-shift blue, * lapis-lazuli-like, like the-colour-of the-sky;
and-I-gazed in the-shift at-her: * a-moon-of the-summer in the-nights-of the-winter.
sentences.i: She came forward in a blue shift, lapis-blue like the colour of the sky; and I gazed upon her in the shift: a summer moon in the nights of winter.
sentences.n: The pointing is as printed. قَمَرُ is nominative where the verb would take an accusative; read it as an exclamation, 'a summer moon ...!', a moon that does not belong to winter nights. The print points فَتَامَّلْتُ with a bare alif, for فَتَأَمَّلْتُ.

sentences.t: قَالَ ثُمَّ غَيَّرُوا تِلْكَ الْبَدْلَةَ بِبَدْلَةٍ غَيْرِهَا وَلَثَّمُوهَا بِفَاضِلِ شَعْرِهَا وَ أَرْخَوْا ذَوَائِبَهَا السُّودَ الطِّوَالَ فَأَشْبَهَ سَوَادُهَا وَطُولُهَا مَا اعْتَكَرَ مِنَ اللَّيَالِي
sentences.tr: qāla thumma ghayyarū tilka al-badlata bi-badlatin ghayrihā wa-laththamūhā bi-fāḍili shaʿrihā wa arkhaw dhawāʾibahā al-sūda al-ṭiwāla fa-ashbaha sawāduhā wa-ṭūluhā mā iʿtakara mina al-layālī
sentences.l: He-said: Then they-changed that the-suit for-a-suit other-than-it, and-muffled-her-mouth with-the-surplus-of her-hair, and let-down her-locks, the-black, the-long, and-her-blackness and-her-length resembled what had-grown-dense of-the-nights.
sentences.i: He said: Then they changed that outfit for a different one, muffled her face with the surplus of her hair, and let down her long black tresses, so that their blackness and length were like the darkest of nights.
sentences.n: The conjunction و stands alone at the end of a printed line, and its verb begins the next; I keep it as a separate word. اعتكر is said of night when it thickens into darkness.

sentences.t: وَرَمَتِ الْقُلُوبَ بِسِهَامِ الْحَدَقِ النَّافِثَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ramati al-qulūba bi-sihāmi al-ḥadaqi al-nāfithati
sentences.l: And-she-shot the-hearts with-arrows-of the-eyes, the-blowing.
sentences.i: And she shot the hearts with arrows from her spell-casting eyes.
sentences.n: نافثة is 'blowing', as sorcerers blow on knots when they cast a spell: eyes that bewitch.

sentences.t: وَجَلَوْهَا الْخِلْعَهَ الثَّالِثَهَ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا الْقَائِلُ شِعْـــــــــــــــــرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-jalawhā al-khilʿaha al-thālithaha ka-mā qāla fīhā al-qāʾilu shiʿrun
sentences.l: And-they-displayed-her the-robe the-third, as said about-her the-sayer, verse:
sentences.i: They displayed her in the third robe, as a poet has said of her in verse:

sentences.t:
وَمُلْتَثِمٌ بِالشَّعْرِ مِنْ فَوْقِ وَجْنَتِهِ * غَدَتْ فِتْنَةً شَبَّهْتُها بِحُمَاتِ
فَقُلْتُ سَتَرْتَ الصُّبْحَ بِاللَّيْلِ قَالَ لَا * لَانِ سَتَــرْتُ الْبَدْرَ بِالظُّلُمَاتِ
sentences.tr:
wa-multathimun bi-al-shaʿri min fawqi wajnatihi * ghadat fitnatan shabbahtuhā bi-ḥumāti
fa-qultu satarta al-ṣubḥa bi-al-layli qāla lā * lāni satartu al-badra bi-al-ẓulumāti
sentences.l:
And a-muffled-one with-the-hair from above his-cheek — * it-became a-temptation; I-likened-it to-stings(?);
and-I-said: You-have-veiled the-dawn with-the-night. He-said: No, * because-I (have) veiled the-full-moon with-the-darknesses.
sentences.i: A youth veiled in hair that falls across his cheek: it became a snare, and I likened it to stinging things. I said, 'You have hidden the morning with the night.' He said, 'No — I have hidden the full moon in the darkness.'
sentences.n: The pointing is as printed. حُمَاتِ closes the first line and its sense is uncertain: it may be the plural of حُمَة, 'sting, venom', or of حَامٍ, 'protector'; 'stings' suits a temptation best. لَانِ is printed for لِأَنِّي, 'because I'. The beloved corrects the poet: his face is the moon, not the dawn, and the hair is the night that hides it.

sentences.t: وَجَلَوْهَا الْخِلْعَهَ الرَّابِعَةَ فَأَقْبَلَتْ كَالشَّمْسِ الطَّالِعَةِ وَتَمَايَلَتْ مِنَ الدَّلَالِ وَتَلَفَّتَتْ كَتَلَفُّةِ الْغِزْلَانِ وَرَشَقَتِ الْقُلُوبَ مِنْ أَجْفَانِهَا بِنِبَالٍ
sentences.tr: wa-jalawhā al-khilʿata al-rābiʿata fa-aqbalat ka-al-shamsi al-ṭāliʿati wa-tamāyalat mina al-dalāli wa-talaffatat ka-talaffuta al-ghizlāni wa-rashaqati al-qulūba min ajfānihā bi-nibālin
sentences.l: And-they-displayed-her the-robe the-fourth, and-she-came-forward like-the-sun the-rising, and-swayed out-of the-coquetry, and-turned-about like-the-turning-about-of the-gazelles, and-pelted the-hearts from her-eyelids with-arrows.
sentences.i: They displayed her in the fourth robe, and she came forward like the rising sun, swayed in her coquetry, glanced about like gazelles, and pelted hearts with arrows from her eyelids.
sentences.n: كتلفة is printed with ة where the verbal noun تلفت would end in ت; I read it as 'like the turning about of the gazelles'.

sentences.t: كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا الْوَاصِفُ شِـــــــــــــعْــــــــــرٌ
sentences.tr: ka-mā qāla fīhā al-wāṣifu shiʿrun
sentences.l: As said about-her the-describer, verse:
sentences.i: As the describer has said of her, in verse:

sentences.t:
وَشَمْسُ حُسْنٍ بَدَتْ لِلنَّاسِ تَنْظُرُها * تَزْهُو بِحُسْنِ دَلَالٍ زَانَهُ خَفَــرُ
مُذْ وَاجَهَتْ بِمُحَيَّاهَا وَمَبْسِمِــها * شَمْسَ النَّهارِ غَدَتْ بِالْغَيْمِ تَسْتَتِرُ
sentences.tr:
wa-shamsu ḥusnin badat li-al-nāsi tanẓuruhā * tazhū bi-ḥusni dalālin zānahu khafaru
mudh wājahat bi-muḥayyāhā wa-mabsimihā * shamsa al-nahāri ghadat bi-al-ghaymi tastatiru
sentences.l:
And a-sun-of beauty appeared to-the-people, you-look-at-her; * she-glows with-the-beauty-of coquetry which modesty adorned;
since she-faced with-her-face and-her-smiling-mouth * the-sun-of the-day, it-went with-the-cloud to-veil-itself.
sentences.i: A sun of beauty appeared before the people, and you gaze upon her. She glows in the loveliness of a coquetry that shyness adorns. Since she confronted the sun of day with her countenance and her smiling lips, it has gone to hide itself behind the clouds.
sentences.n: The pointing is as printed. In the second line شَمْسَ النَّهارِ is the object of 'confronted' and the subject of 'hides': the real sun, put to shame by her, takes cover in cloud.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَطَلَعَتْ فِى الْخِلْعَةِ الْخَامِسَةِ كَالصَّبِيَّةِ الْأَنِيسَةِ كَأَنَّهَا قَضِيبَ بَانٍ أَوْ غَزَالٍ عَطْشَانَ وَقَدْ دَبَّتْ عَقَارِبُهَا وَأَبْدَتْ عَجَائِبَهَا وَهَزَّتْ أَرْدَافَهَا وَأَشْهَرَتْ سَوَالِفَهَا
sentences.tr: qāla wa-ṭalaʿat fī al-khilʿati al-khāmisati ka-al-ṣabiyyati al-anīsati ka-annahā qaḍība bānin aw ghazālin ʿaṭshāna wa-qad dabbat ʿaqāribuhā wa-abdat ʿajāʾibahā wa-hazzat ardāfahā wa-ashharat sawālifahā
sentences.l: He-said: and-she-came-forth in the-robe the-fifth like-the-girl the-sociable, as-if-she (were) a-branch-of ban or a-gazelle thirsty, and-her-scorpions crept, and-she-showed her-wonders, and-shook her-hips, and-displayed her-sidelocks.
sentences.i: He said: And she came forth in the fifth robe, like a gentle young girl, as though she were a bough of the ban-tree or a thirsty gazelle; her curls crept, she showed her marvels, shook her hips, and bared the sides of her neck.
sentences.n: Her 'scorpions' are the curled locks at the temples, which sting like a scorpion's tail. سوالف is either the side-locks or the sides of the neck; 'displayed' fits both. After كأنها I point the accusative of Classical Arabic; the print gives no endings.

sentences.t: كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا وَاصِفِيهَا شِـــــــــــعْـــــــــرٌ
sentences.tr: ka-mā qāla fīhā wāṣifīhā shiʿrun
sentences.l: As said about-her her-describers, verse:
sentences.i: As those who describe her have said, in verse:
sentences.n: واصفيها has the oblique ending -ī where the subject of قال should be واصفوها; Middle Arabic often keeps one plural form for every case.

sentences.t:
تَبَدَّتْ كَبَدْرِ التِّمِّ فِي لَيْلَةِ السَّعْدِ * مُنَعَّمَةَ الاَطْرَافِ مَمْشُوقَــةَ الْقَدِّ
لِها مُقْلَةٌ تَسْبِي الْاَنَامَ بِحُسْنِها * وَقَدْ حَكَتِ الْيَاقُوتَ فِي حُمْرَةِ الْخَدِّ
تَحَدَّرُ فَوْقَ الرِّدْفِ اَسْوَدَ شَعْرِها * فَإِيَّاكَ وَالْحَيَّاتِ مِنْ شَعْرِها الْجَعْدِ
وَقَدْ لَانَتِ الْاَعْطَافُ مِنْها وَقَلْبُها * عَلَى لِينِها اَقْسَى مِنَ الْحَجَرِ الصَّلْدِ
وَتُرْسِلُ سَهْمَ اللَّحْظِ مِنْ فَوْقِ حَاجِبٍ * يُصِيبُ وَلَا يُخْطِي وَإِنْ كَانَ مِنْ بُعْدِ
اِذَا مَا اعْتَنَقْنَا وَالْتَزَمْتُ وِشَاحَها * يُدَافِعُنِي عَنْ ضَمِّها ذَلِكَ النَّهْدِ
فَيَا حُسْنَها قَدْ فَاقَ كُلَّ مُلَاحَــةٍ * وَيَا قَدَّها اَزْرَيْتَ بِالْغُصْنِ الْمُلْدِ
sentences.tr:
tabaddat ka-badri al-timmi fī laylati al-saʿdi * munaʿʿamata al-aṭrāfi mamshūqata al-qaddi
lihā muqlatun tasbī al-anāma bi-ḥusnihā * wa-qad ḥakati al-yāqūta fī ḥumrati al-khaddi
taḥaddaru fawqa al-ridfi aswada shaʿrihā * fa-iyyāka wa-al-ḥayyāti min shaʿrihā al-jaʿdi
wa-qad lānati al-aʿṭāfu minhā wa-qalbuhā * ʿalā līnihā aqsā mina al-ḥajari al-ṣaldi
wa-tursilu sahma al-laḥẓi min fawqi ḥājibin * yuṣību wa-lā yukhṭī wa-in kāna min buʿdi
idhā mā iʿtanaqnā wa-iltazamtu wishāḥahā * yudāfiʿunī ʿan ḍammihā dhālika al-nahdi
fa-yā ḥusnahā qad fāqa kulla mulāḥatin * wa-yā qaddahā azrayta bi-al-ghuṣni al-muldi
sentences.i: She appeared like the full moon at its fullness on a night of good fortune, soft of limb, slender and shapely of figure. She has an eye that takes mankind captive with its beauty, and it rivals the ruby in the redness of the cheek. Her black hair streams down over her hips, so beware of the snakes of her curling locks. Her flanks are soft, yet her heart, for all its softness, is harder than flint. She sends the arrow of her glance from over a brow; it never misses, though it be from far off. When we embrace and I take hold of her sash, that breast of hers holds me off from clasping her. O her beauty, that has surpassed every loveliness! And O her figure, you have put to shame the tender bough!
sentences.n: The pointing is as printed, including a few words marked only in part (لِها, بِحُسْنِها). ذَلِكَ النَّهْدِ ends in a genitive where grammar wants a nominative (النَّهْدُ), kept as printed, doubtless for the rhyme in -di. تَحَدَّرُ is a short form of تَتَحَدَّرُ. الْمُلْدِ is obscure to me: perhaps the plural form of أَمْلَد, 'soft, tender', here describing the branch. 'The snakes' are her curling locks; 'beware of them' is a lover's jest.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَجَلَوْهَا الْخِلْعَهَ السَّادِسَهَ فِي خِلْعَةٍ خَضْرَاءَ فَأَزْرَتْ بِقَوَامِهَا الصَّعْدَةَ السَّمْرَاءَ
sentences.tr: qāla wa-jalawhā al-khilʿaha al-sādisaha fī khilʿatin khaḍrāʾa fa-azrat bi-qawāmihā al-ṣaʿdata al-samrāʾa
sentences.l: He-said: and-they-displayed-her the-robe the-sixth in-a-robe green, and-she-put-to-shame by-her-stature the-lance, the-brown.
sentences.i: He said: Then they displayed her in the sixth robe, a green one, and her slender figure put the tawny lance to shame.
sentences.n: The ṣaʿda is a spear-shaft of straight cane, a standard image for a slender, upright figure; 'brown' is its colour.

sentences.t: وَفَاقَتْ بِجَمَالِهَا مِلَاحَ الْآفَاقِ وَأَزْهَرَتْ بِإِشْرَاقِ وَجْهِهَا عَلَى بَدْرِ الْإِشْرَاقِ
sentences.tr: wa-fāqat bi-jamālihā milāḥa al-āfāqi wa-azharat bi-ishrāqi wajhihā ʿalā badri al-ishrāqi
sentences.l: And-she-surpassed by-her-beauty the-fair-ones-of the-horizons, and-bloomed with-the-radiance-of her-face over the-full-moon-of the-radiance.
sentences.i: She surpassed in her beauty the fair ones of every horizon, and the radiance of her face outshone the full moon at its brightest.
sentences.n: The print has الافاق with a single alif; the madda sign marks the long ā that the hamza and alif of الآفاق make together. بدر الاشراق, 'moon of radiance', is a high-flown phrase for the full moon; إشراق also means sunrise.

sentences.t: وَنَالَتْ مِنَ الْجَمَالِ أَمَانِيَهَا وَسَبَتِ الْغُصُونَ بِأَيْنِهَا وَتَثَنِّيهَا وَفَتَّتِ الْكُبُودَ بِحُسْنِ مَعَانِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-nālat mina al-jamāli amāniyahā wa-sabati al-ghuṣūna bi-aynihā wa-tathannīhā wa-fattati al-kubūda bi-ḥusni maʿānīhā
sentences.l: And-she-attained from the-beauty her-wishes, and-captivated the-branches with-her-languor and-her-bending, and-crumbled the-livers with-the-beauty-of her-subtleties.
sentences.i: She won from beauty all she could wish, captivated the boughs with her languor and her swaying, and melted the hearts' livers with the beauty of her subtle graces.
sentences.n: باينها is probably a misprint for بلينها, 'with her suppleness', which pairs naturally with تثنيها, 'her bending'; as printed it reads بِأَيْنِهَا, ayn being 'languor, weariness', also a beauty's pose, and I point it so. 'Melting the livers' is the idiom for breaking hearts.

sentences.t: كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا بَعْضُ وَاصِفِيهَا شِعْـــــــرٌ
sentences.tr: ka-mā qāla fīhā baʿḍu wāṣifīhā shiʿrun
sentences.l: As said about-her some-of her-describers, verse:
sentences.i: As one of her describers has said, in verse:

sentences.t:
وَجَارِيَةٍ قَدْ اَدَّبَتْهَا الشَّطَارَة * تَرَى الشَّمْسَ مِنْ خَدِّهَا مُسْتَعَارَة
اَتَتْ فِي قَمِيصٍ لَهَا اَخْضَـرِ * كَمَا سَتَرَ الْوَرَقُ بِالْجُلَّنَارَة
فَقُلْنَا لَهَا مَا اسْمُ ذَاكَ اللِّبَاس * فَقَالَتْ كَلَّا مَا مَلِيحَ الْعِبَارَة
شَقَقْنَا مَرَا يُرَ قَوْمٍ بِهِ * فَنَحْنُ نُسَمِّيهِ شَقَّ الْمَرَارَة
sentences.tr:
wa-jāriyatin qad addabathā al-shaṭārah * tarā al-shamsa min khaddihā mustaʿārah
atat fī qamīṣin lahā akhḍari * ka-mā satara al-waraqu bi-al-julnārah
fa-qulnā lahā mā ismu dhāka al-libās * fa-qālat kallā mā malīḥa al-ʿibārah
shaqaqnā marā yura qawmin bihi * fa-naḥnu nusammīhi shaqqa al-marārah
sentences.i: A girl whom cleverness has schooled; you see the sun borrowing its glow from her cheek. She came in a shift of hers, a green one, as the leaves screen the pomegranate blossom. We said to her, 'What is the name of that garment?' She said, 'No, you of the fine phrase! We split the gall-bladders of a whole people with it, and so we call it "Split-the-Gall".'
sentences.n: The pointing is as printed; the last word of each line has no case ending. The joke is in the colour: bile is green, so the green shift is called شَقّ المرارة, 'splitting of the gall', since it frightens people to death; the print splits مَرَائِرَ into مَرَا يُرَ. The answer to the question is only reached in the last line. In 'kallā mā malīḥa', the accusative malīḥa is what a vocative يَا مَلِيحَ would give, so I read ما as a misprint for يا; if it is meant as an exclamation, 'how fine the phrase!', the sense is nearly the same.

sentences.t: وَجَلَوْهَا فِي الْخِلْعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ بَيْنَ مُعَصْفَرٍ وَمُزَعْفَرٍ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا بَعْضُ وَاصِفِهَا —
sentences.tr: wa-jalawhā fī al-khilʿati al-sābiʿati bayna muʿaṣfarin wa-muzaʿfarin kamā qāla fīhā baʿḍu wāṣifihā —
sentences.l: And-they-displayed-her in the-robe the-seventh, between safflower-dyed and-saffron-dyed, as said about-her some-of her-describers:
sentences.i: They displayed her in the seventh robe, between the safflower-red and the saffron-yellow, as one of her describers has said of her:

sentences.t:
وَتَمِيسُ بَيْنَ مُزَعْفَرٍ وَمُعَصْفَرِ * وَمُعَنْبَرٍ وَمُمَسَّكٍ وَمُصَنْدَلِ
هَيْفَاءُ اِنْ قَالَ الشَّبَابُ لَهَا انْهَضِي * قَالَتْ رَوَادِفُها اقْعُدِي وَتَمَهَّلِي
وَاِذَا سَالَتْ الْوَصْلَ قَالَ جَمَالُهَا * جُودِي وَقَالَ دَلَالُهَا لَاتَفْعَلِي
sentences.tr:
wa-tamīsu bayna muzaʿfarin wa-muʿaṣfari * wa-muʿanbarin wa-mumassakin wa-muṣandali
hayfāʾu in qāla al-shabābu lahā inhaḍī * qālat rawādifuhā iqʿudī wa-tamahhalī
wa-idhā saʾalat al-waṣla qāla jamāluhā * jūdī wa-qāla dalāluhā lā-tafʿalī
sentences.i: She sways between saffron-dyed silks and safflower-red, and silks scented with ambergris, with musk, with sandalwood. Slender-waisted: if the young men say to her "Rise," her hips say, "Sit, and take your time." And when she asks for union, her beauty says, "Be generous," and her coquetry says, "Do not."
sentences.n: The edition points these lines and the pointing is kept as printed. Note that اِنْ and وَاِذَا are printed with a bare alif and kasra, with no hamza. سَالَتْ is printed without hamza and read saʾalat, "she asked"; the sense may rather be سَأَلْتَ, "you ask" (the beloved's beauty bidding her yield to the asker), but the print's pointing is followed. لَاتَفْعَلِي is printed as one word, lā tafʿalī, "do not". رَوَادِفُها has its last word-part unpointed in the print. The joke of the poem is the pull between the young men's urging and her body's languor.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْعَرُوسَةُ فَإِنَّهَا لَمَّا فَتَحَتْ عَيْنَهَا قَالَتْ اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ هَٰذَا بَعْلِي وَأَرِحْنِي مِنْ هَٰذَا السَّائِسِ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-ʿarūsatu fa-innahā lammā fataḥat ʿaynahā qālat Allāhumma ijʿal hādhā baʿlī wa-ariḥnī min hādhā al-sāʾisi al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: And-as-for the-bride, then-indeed-she when she-opened her-eye said: "O-God, make this-one my-husband, and-give-me-rest from this the-groom the-hunchback."
sentences.i: As for the bride, when she opened her eyes she said, "O God, make this man my husband, and spare me this hunchbacked groom."
sentences.n: الْعَرُوسَةُ is the colloquial form for the Classical عَرُوس, "bride"; it recurs throughout. وَأَرِحْنِي is from أَرَاحَ, "give rest to, relieve": "relieve me of this groom". (If the print dropped a mīm, it would be وَارْحَمْنِي, "have mercy on me"; the sense of rest suits the context better.)

sentences.t: وَصَارُوا يَجْلُوا الْعَرُوسَةَ إِلَى آخِرِ السَّبْعِ خِلَعٍ عَلَى بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ الْبَصْرِيِّ وَالسَّائِسُ الْأَحْدَبُ جَالِسٌ وَحْدَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārū yajlū al-ʿarūsata ilā ākhiri al-sabʿi khilaʿin ʿalā badri al-dīni ḥasanin al-baṣriyyi wa-al-sāʾisu al-aḥdabu jālisun waḥdahu
sentences.l: And-they-became they-display the-bride up-to the-end-of the-seven robes, before Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan the-Baṣran; and-the-groom the-hunchback sitting alone-of-him.
sentences.i: And they went on displaying the bride, robe after robe, to the end of the seven robes, before Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan of Basra, while the hunchbacked groom sat by himself.
sentences.n: يَجْلُوا has lost its final nūn (Classical يَجْلُونَ); the print often drops it. صَارُوا with an imperfect means "they went on, they began to". وَحْدَةُ is printed with tāʾ marbūṭa where the pronoun -hu is meant; read waḥdahu, "by himself". السَّبْعِ خِلَعٍ puts the article on the number and leaves the noun bare, as often in Middle Arabic. عَلَى here means "in the presence of, before".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغُوا مِنْ ذَٰلِكَ أَذِنُوا لِلنَّاسِ بِالِانْصِرٰفِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghū min dhālika adhinū li-al-nāsi bi-al-inṣirāfi
sentences.l: And-when they-finished from that, they-gave-leave to-the-people for-the-departing.
sentences.i: When they had finished with that, they gave the people leave to go.
sentences.n: بِالِانْصِرٰفِ is printed without the alif of inṣirāf; the dagger alif supplies it.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ جَمِيعُ مَنْ كَانَ فِي الْفَرَحِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْأَوْلَادِ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ إِلَّا بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ وَالسَّائِسُ الْأَحْدَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja jamīʿu man kāna fī al-faraḥi mina al-nisāʾi wa-al-awlādi wa-lam yabqa illā badru al-dīni ḥasanun wa-al-sāʾisu al-aḥdabu
sentences.l: And-went-out all-of whoever was in the-wedding, of the-women and-the-children; and-did-not remain except Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan and-the-groom the-hunchback.
sentences.i: Everyone who had been at the wedding went out, women and children alike, and none stayed behind but Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan and the hunchbacked groom.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَوَاشِطَ أَدْخَلُوا الْعَرُوسَةَ لِيُغَيِّرُوا مَا عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْحُلِيِّ وَالْحُلَلِ وَيَجْعَلُوهَا لِلْعَرِيسِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-mawāshiṭa adkhalū al-ʿarūsata li-yughayyirū mā ʿalayhā mina al-ḥuliyyi wa-al-ḥulali wa-yajʿalūhā li-al-ʿarīsi
sentences.l: Then indeed the-hairdresser-women brought-in the-bride in-order-to-change what is-on-her of the-jewels and-the-robes, and-make-her for-the-bridegroom.
sentences.i: Then the dressers led the bride in, to change the jewels and robes she wore and make her ready for the bridegroom.
sentences.n: الْمَوَاشِط (sing. مَاشِطَة) are the women who dress, comb and adorn the bride. The verb أَدْخَلُوا is masculine plural for a group of women, as often in the print.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ تَقَدَّمَ السَّائِسُ الْأَحْدَبُ إِلَى بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ وَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي آنَسْتَنَا اللَّيْلَةَ وَغَمَرْتَنَا بِإِحْسَانِكَ فَمَا تَقُومُ تَرُوحُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqaddama al-sāʾisu al-aḥdabu ilā badri al-dīni ḥasanin wa-qāla yā sayyidī ānastanā al-layla wa-ghamartanā bi-iḥsānika fa-mā taqūmu tarūḥu
sentences.l: So at that, came-forward the-groom the-hunchback to Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan and-said: "O my-master, you-kept-us-company the-night, and-you-overwhelmed-us with-your-kindness; so-not you-rise you-go?"
sentences.i: Then the hunchbacked groom came forward to Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan and said, "My master, you have kept us company tonight and loaded us with your kindness. Will you not get up and go?"
sentences.n: فَمَا تَقُومُ تَرُوحُ is colloquial: two imperfects side by side with no "and", "why don't you get up (and) go?". The groom is politely dismissing him so that he can be alone with the bride.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ قَامَ وَخَرَجَ مِنَ الْبَابِ فَلَقِيَهُ الْعِفْرِيتُ فَقَالَ لَهُ قِفْ يَا بَدْرَالدِّينِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla bi-smi Allāhi thumma qāma wa-kharaja mina al-bābi fa-laqiyahu al-ʿifrītu fa-qāla lahu qif yā badra al-dīni
sentences.l: And-he-said "In the-name-of God", then he-rose and-went-out from the-door, and-met-him the-ifrit, and-said to-him: "Stop, O Badr-al-Dīn."
sentences.i: He said, "In God's name," then rose and went out of the door; but the ifrit met him and said, "Stop, Badr al-Dīn."

sentences.t: فَإِذَا خَرَجَ الْأَحْدَبُ أَىْ بَيْتِ الرَّاحَةِ ادْخُلْ أَنْتَ وَلَا تَتَوَقَّفْ وَاجْلِسْ فِي الْبَشْخَانَةِ.
sentences.tr: fa-idhā kharaja al-aḥdabu ay bayti al-rāḥati udkhul anta wa-lā tatawaqqaf wa-ajlis fī al-bashkhānati.
sentences.l: So-when goes-out the-hunchback to house-of the-rest, enter you, and-do-not linger, and-sit in the-bashkhāna.
sentences.i: When the hunchback goes off to the privy, go in yourself, don't hang back, and sit down in the inner chamber.
sentences.n: أَيْ is printed اى; here it stands for إِلَى, "to", and so again below (اى فوق). It is not the usual أَيْ, "that is". بَيْتُ الرَّاحَةِ, "house of rest", is the privy. الْبَشْخَانَة (bashkhāna) is the room where bride and groom will meet; the word is obscure (perhaps Persian-Turkish) and "inner chamber" is a guess from context.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا أَقْبَلَتِ الْعَرُوسَةُ فَقُلْ لَهَا أَنَا زَوْجُكِ وَالْمَلِكُ إِنَّمَا عَمِلَ هَٰذِهِ الْحِيلَةَ خَوْفًا عَلَيْكِ مِنَ الْعَيْنِ وَهَٰذَا الَّذِي رَأَيْتِهِ سَائِسٌ مِنْ سُيَّا سِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā aqbalati al-ʿarūsatu fa-qul lahā anā zawjuki wa-al-maliku innamā ʿamila hādhihi al-ḥīlata khawfan ʿalayki mina al-ʿayni wa-hādhā alladhī raʾaytihi sāʾisun min suyyā sinā
sentences.l: So-when approaches the-bride, then-say to-her: "I your-husband; and-the-king only made this the-ruse, fear for-you from the-eye; and-this-one whom you-saw (is) a-groom from our-grooms."
sentences.i: When the bride comes in, say to her, "I am your husband. The king contrived all this only out of fear for you, to ward off the evil eye; and the man you saw is one of our grooms."
sentences.n: سُيَّا سِنَا is printed as two words; it is one word, سُيَّاسِنَا, "our grooms" (suyyās, a colloquial plural of sāʾis). الْعَيْن is the evil eye. The ifrit scripts a ruse for Badr al-Dīn to pass himself off as the husband.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبِلْ عَلَيْهَا وَاكْشِفْ وَجْهَهَا فَنَحْنُ لَحِقَتْنَا الْغَيْرَةُ مِنْ هَٰذَا الْأَمْرِ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbil ʿalayhā wa-akshif wajhahā fa-naḥnu laḥiqatnā al-ghayratu min hādhā al-amri
sentences.l: Then turn upon-her and-uncover her-face; for-we, overtook-us the-jealousy from this the-matter.
sentences.i: Then turn to her and unveil her face; for jealousy has overtaken us over this business.

sentences.t: فِيمَا بَدْرُالدِّينِ يَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَ الْعِفْرِيتِ وَإِذَا بِالسَّائِسِ خَارِجٌ وَدَخَلَ بَيْتَ الرَّاحَةِ وَقَعَدَ عَلَى الْكُرْسِيِّ وَطَلَعَ لَهُ الْعِفْرِيتُ مِنَ الْحَوْضِ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْمَاءُ فِى صِفَةِ فَارٍ وَقَالَ زِيقْ
sentences.tr: fīmā badru al-dīni yataḥaddathu maʿa al-ʿifrīti wa-idhā bi-al-sāʾisi khārijun wa-dakhala bayta al-rāḥati wa-qaʿada ʿalā al-kursiyyi wa-ṭalaʿa lahu al-ʿifrītu mina al-ḥawḍi alladhī fīhi al-māʾu fī ṣifati fārin wa-qāla zīq
sentences.l: While Badr-al-Dīn conversing with the-ifrit, and-behold with-the-groom going-out; and-he-entered house-of the-rest and-sat on the-chair; and-came-up to-him the-ifrit from the-basin which in-it the-water, in form-of a-mouse, and-said: "Zīq."
sentences.i: While Badr al-Dīn was talking with the ifrit, the groom came out and went into the privy and sat down on the seat; and the ifrit rose up before him out of the water-basin in the shape of a mouse and squeaked, "Zīq!"
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِ is "and behold": the بِ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what appears, here السَّائِس. In English the whole run is one scene; the print strings the verbs together with "and". The sounds زِيقْ, مِيَا, عَوْهْ, هَاقْ have no fixed Arabic form; the pointing is ours and only an approximation of the sound.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْأَحْدَبُ مَا حَالُكَ فَكَبُرَ الْفَارُ حَتَّى صَارَ قِطًّا وَقَالَ مِيَا مِيَا وَكَبُرَ حَتَّى صَارَ كَلْبًا وَقَالَ عَوْهْ عَوْهْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-aḥdabu mā ḥāluka fa-kabura al-fāru ḥattā ṣāra qiṭṭan wa-qāla miyā miyā wa-kabura ḥattā ṣāra kalban wa-qāla ʿawh ʿawh
sentences.l: And-said the-hunchback: "What your-state?" And-grew-big the-mouse until it-became a-cat, and-said: "Miyā, miyā"; and-grew-big until it-became a-dog, and-said: "ʿAwh, ʿawh."
sentences.i: The hunchback said, "What ails you?" And the mouse swelled until it became a cat, and said, "Meow, meow"; and swelled until it became a dog, and said, "Woof, woof."

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ السَّائِسُ ذَٰلِكَ فَزِعَ وَقَالَ اخْسَأْ يَا مَشُومُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara al-sāʾisu dhālika faziʿa wa-qāla ikhsaʾ yā mashūmu
sentences.l: And-when saw the-groom that, he-was-terrified and-said: "Begone, O ill-omened!"
sentences.i: When the groom saw that, he took fright and said, "Begone, you ill-omened thing!"
sentences.n: مَشُوم is printed for مَشْؤُوم, "ill-omened". اخْسَأْ is the word shouted at a dog to drive it off.

sentences.t: وَالْكَلْبُ كَبُرَ وَانْتَفَخَ حَتَّى صَارَ جَحْشًا وَنَهَقَ وَصَرَخَ فِي وَجْهِهِ هَاقْ هَاقْ فَانْزَعَجَ فَقَالَ اِلْحَقُونِي يَا أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-kalbu kabura wa-intafakha ḥattā ṣāra jaḥshan wa-nahaqa wa-ṣarakha fī wajhihi hāq hāq fa-inzaʿaja fa-qāla ilḥaqūnī yā ahla al-bayti
sentences.l: And-the-dog grew-big and-swelled-up until it-became a-donkey-foal, and-brayed and-cried-out in his-face "Hāq, hāq"; and-he-was-startled, and-said: "Come-to-me, O people-of the-house!"
sentences.i: The dog swelled and grew until it became a young ass, and brayed and screamed in his face, "Hee-haw, hee-haw!" He was thrown into a panic and cried, "Help me, people of the house!"

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْحِمَارِ كَبُرَ وَصَارَ قَدْرَ الْجَامُوسَةِ وَسَدَّ عَلَيْهِ الْمَكَانَ وَتَكَلَّمَ بِكَلَامِ ابْنِ آدَمَ وَقَالَ وَيْلَكَ يَا أَحْدَبُ يَا أَنْتَنُ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-ḥimāri kabura wa-ṣāra qadra al-jāmūsati wa-sadda ʿalayhi al-makāna wa-takallama bi-kalāmi ibni ādama wa-qāla waylaka yā aḥdabu yā antanu
sentences.l: And-behold with-the-donkey: it-grew-big and-became the-size-of the-buffalo-cow, and-blocked on-him the-place, and-spoke with-the-speech-of son-of Adam, and-said: "Woe-to-you, O hunchback, O most-stinking!"
sentences.i: And behold, the donkey grew until it was as big as a buffalo-cow, and filled the whole place around him, and spoke in human speech, saying, "Curse you, hunchback, you stinking wretch!"
sentences.n: ابْنُ آدَمَ, "son of Adam", is simply "a human being". وَسَدَّ عَلَيْهِ الْمَكَانَ is "blocked the place on him", that is, it filled the space so that he was hemmed in.

sentences.t: وَالسَّائِسُ لَحِقَتْهُ الْبَطْنُ وَقَعَدَ عَلَى الْمَلَاقِي بِأَثْوَابِهِ وَاشْتَبَكَتْ أَسْنَانُهُ بَعْضُهَا بِبَعْضٍ
sentences.tr: wa-al-sāʾisu laḥiqathu al-baṭnu wa-qaʿada ʿalā al-malāqī bi-athwābihi wa-ishtabakat asnānuhu baʿḍuhā bi-baʿḍin
sentences.l: And-the-groom, overtook-him the-belly, and-he-sat on the-malāqī in-his-garments, and-interlocked his-teeth, some-of-them with-some.
sentences.i: As for the groom, his bowels seized him; he sat down on the privy-seat just as he was, in his clothes, and his teeth clenched together, one upon another.
sentences.n: لَحِقَتْهُ الْبَطْنُ has a feminine verb with الْبَطْن, which is usually masculine: "the belly caught him", that is, fright loosened his bowels. الْمَلَاقِي is obscure: it looks like a plural of مَلْقًى, "place where something is thrown", and here it is the privy hole or seat (the ifrit later pushes his head into it).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْعِفْرِيتُ قُلْ ضَاقَتْ عَلَيْكَ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا وَجَدْتَ تَتَزَوَّجُ إِلَّا بِمَعْشُوقَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-ʿifrītu qul ḍāqat ʿalayka al-dunyā wa-mā wajadta tatazawwaju illā bi-maʿshūqatī
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-ifrit: "Say: grew-narrow on-you the-world, and-you-did-not-find you-marry except with-my-beloved?"
sentences.i: The ifrit said to him, "Tell me, was the world too narrow for you, that you could find no one to marry but my beloved?"
sentences.n: There is no question word in the print; the question is carried by the tone. تَزَوَّجَ بِـ, "marry", with بِ is the Middle Arabic construction (Classical takes the direct object).

sentences.t: فَسَكَتَ فَقَالَ لَهُ رُدَّالْجَوَابَ وَإِلَّا أَسْكَنْتُكَ التُّرَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-sakata fa-qāla lahu rudda al-jawāba wa-illā askantuka al-turāba
sentences.l: And-he-fell-silent; and-said to-him: "Give-back the-answer, or-else I-lodged-you the-dust."
sentences.i: He fell silent. The ifrit said to him, "Answer me, or I will lay you in the dust."
sentences.n: أَسْكَنْتُكَ is a past tense for a future threat, as in a conditional.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ مَايِ ذَنْبٌ إِلَّا أَنَّهُمْ غَصَبُونِي وَمَا عَرَفْتُ أَنَّ لَهَا عُشَّاقَ جَوَامِيسَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi māy dhanbun illā annahum ghaṣabūnī wa-mā ʿaraftu anna lahā ʿushshāqa jawāmīsa
sentences.l: And-he-said: "By-God, no-fault-of-mine except that-they forced-me; and-I-did-not know that to-her are lovers, buffaloes."
sentences.i: He said, "By God, I am not to blame, except that they forced me into it; and I did not know she had lovers — buffaloes at that!"
sentences.n: ماي ذنب is printed so; it is most likely مَا لِي ذَنْبٌ, "I have no fault", with the lām dropped (read here as mā-y). عُشَّاقَ جَوَامِيسَ is unclear: either "lovers of buffaloes" or, with the second noun in apposition, "lovers who are buffaloes", a joke on the ifrit's last shape. The latter is followed here.

sentences.t: وَلَٰكِنْ أَنَا تَائِبٌ إِلَى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin anā tāʾibun ilā Allāhi thumma ilayka
sentences.l: But I repentant to God, then to-you.
sentences.i: But I turn in repentance to God, and then to you.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْعِفْرِيتُ أُقْسِمُ عَلَيْكَ إِنْ خَرَجْتَ هَٰذَا الْوَقْتَ مِنْ هَٰذَا الْمَوْضِعِ أَوْ تَكَلَّمْتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ قَتَلْتُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-ʿifrītu uqsimu ʿalayka in kharajta hādhā al-waqta min hādhā al-mawḍiʿi aw takallamta qabla an taṭluʿa al-shamsu qataltuka
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-ifrit: "I-adjure you: if you-go-out this the-time from this the-place, or you-speak before that rises the-sun, I-killed-you."
sentences.i: The ifrit said to him, "I swear to you: if you leave this place at this hour, or speak before the sun rises, I will kill you."
sentences.n: قَتَلْتُكَ, "I killed you", is a past tense used for a sure future result after the condition. أُقْسِمُ عَلَيْكَ is "I adjure you", a solemn warning.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ اخْرُجْ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِكَ وَلَا تَعُدْ إِلَى هَٰذَا الْبَيْتِ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā ṭalaʿati al-shamsu ukhruj ilā ḥāli sabīlika wa-lā taʿud ilā hādhā al-bayti abadan
sentences.l: So-when rose the-sun, go-out to state-of your-way, and-do-not return to this the-house ever.
sentences.i: When the sun has risen, go on your way, and never come back to this house.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعِفْرِيتَ مَسَكَ السَّائِسَ الْأَحْدَبَ وَقَلَبَ رَأْسَهُ فِى الْمَلَاقِي وَجَعَلَهُ إِلَى تَحْتُ وَجَعَلَ رِجْلَيْهِ أَىْ فَوْقُ وَقَالَ لَهُ أُخَلِّيكَ هُنَا أَنَا حَارِسُكَ إِلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿifrīta masaka al-sāʾisa al-aḥdaba wa-qalaba raʾsahu fī al-malāqī wa-jaʿalahu ilā taḥtu wa-jaʿala rijlayhi ay fawqu wa-qāla lahu ukhallīka hunā anā ḥārisuka ilā ṭulūʿi al-shamsi
sentences.l: Then indeed the-ifrit seized the-groom the-hunchback, and-turned-over his-head in the-malāqī, and-put-him to below, and-put his-two-legs to above, and-said to-him: "I-leave-you here; I your-guard until rising-of the-sun."
sentences.i: Then the ifrit seized the hunchbacked groom, thrust his head down into the privy-hole and turned him upside down with his legs in the air, and said, "I leave you here; I will stand guard over you until the sun rises."
sentences.n: إِلَى تَحْتُ and أَيْ فَوْقُ are "down" and "up", the adverbs taking a final damma. Again أَيْ is the print's اى for إِلَى.

sentences.t: هَٰذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ قِصَّةِ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min qiṣṣati al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: This (is) what was of the-story-of the-hunchback.
sentences.i: That is what happened in the hunchback's story.
sentences.n: هَٰذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ ... وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ ... is the stock formula for switching between two lines of a story: "that is what happened to X; as for what happened to Y ...".

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ قِصَّةِ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ الْبَصْرِيِّ فَإِنَّهُ خَلَّى الْأَحْدَبَ وَالْعِفْرِيتَ يَتَخَاصَمَانِ وَدَخَلَ الْبَيْتَ وَجَلَسَ فِي وَسْطِ الْبَشْخَانَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min qiṣṣati badri al-dīni ḥasanin al-baṣriyyi fa-innahu khallā al-aḥdaba wa-al-ʿifrīta yatakhāṣamāni wa-dakhala al-bayta wa-jalasa fī wasṭi al-bashkhānati
