sentences.l: And-as-for what was of the-story-of Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan the-Baṣran, then-indeed-he left the-hunchback and-the-ifrit quarrelling, and-entered the-house and-sat in middle-of the-bashkhāna.
sentences.i: As for Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan of Basra, he left the hunchback and the ifrit to their quarrel, went into the room and sat down in the middle of the inner chamber.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْعَرُوسَةِ أَقْبَلَتْ وَمَعَهَا عَجُوزٌ فَوَقَفَتْ فِي بَابِ الْبَيْتِ وَقَالَتْ يَا أَبَا الْقَوَامِ قُمْ خُذْ وَدَاعَةَ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-ʿarūsati aqbalat wa-maʿahā ʿajūzun fa-waqafat fī bābi al-bayti wa-qālat yā abā al-qawāmi qum khudh wadāʿata Allāhi
sentences.l: And-behold with-the-bride: she-came-on, and-with-her an-old-woman; and-she-stood in door-of the-house, and-said: "O father-of the-stature, rise, take God's trust."
sentences.i: And behold, the bride came in, with an old woman beside her, who stopped at the door of the room and said, "Abū al-Qawām, get up and take what God has entrusted to you."
sentences.n: يَا أَبَا الْقَوَامِ, literally "father of the stature", is a form of address for the bridegroom; its exact sense is uncertain. وَدَاعَةُ اللَّهِ, "God's trust", is the bride handed over to her husband (the usual noun for a deposit is وَدِيعَة; وَدَاعَة also means "quietness", and the idiom may play on that).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَلَّتِ الْعَجُوزُ وَدَخَلَتِ الْعَرُوسَةُ فِي دَاخِلِ الْبَشْخَانَةِ وَكَانَ اسْمُهَا سِتَّ الْحُسْنِ وَقَلْبُهَا مَكْسُورٌ
sentences.tr: thumma wallati al-ʿajūzu wa-dakhalati al-ʿarūsatu fī dākhili al-bashkhānati wa-kāna ismuhā sitta al-ḥusni wa-qalbuhā maksūrun
sentences.l: Then turned-away the-old-woman, and-entered the-bride in inside-of the-bashkhāna; and-her-name was Sitt al-Ḥusn (Lady-of the-Beauty), and-her-heart (was) broken.
sentences.i: Then the old woman went away and the bride entered the inner chamber. Her name was Sitt al-Ḥusn, and her heart was broken.
sentences.n: سِتُّ الْحُسْنِ is "Lady of Beauty"; the name stands in the accusative here as the predicate of كَانَ.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ مَا أُمَكِّنُهُ مِنْ نَفْسِي وَلَوْ قَتَلَ رُوحِي
sentences.tr: wa-qālat wa-Allāhi mā umakkinuhu min nafsī wa-law qatala rūḥī
sentences.l: And-she-said: "By-God, I-will-not give-him-power from my-self, even-if he-kill my-soul."
sentences.i: And she said, "By God, I will not give myself to him, even if he takes my life."
sentences.n: مَكَّنَهُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ, "give someone power over one's person", is the idiom for letting someone have one's body. She thinks she is speaking of the hunchback.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَتْ إِلَى دَاخِلِ الْبَشْخَانَةِ نَظَرَتْ بَدْرَالدِّينِ فَقَالَتْ حَبِيبِي إِلَى هَٰذَا الْوَقْتِ قَاعِدٌ لَقَدْ قُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي لَكَ وَلِلسَّائِسِ الْأَحْدَبِ شِرْكَةٌ فِيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalat ilā dākhili al-bashkhānati naẓarat badra al-dīni fa-qālat ḥabībī ilā hādhā al-waqti qāʿidun laqad qultu fī nafsī laka wa-li-al-sāʾisi al-aḥdabi shirkatun fiyya
sentences.l: So-when she-entered to inside-of the-bashkhāna, she-looked-at Badr-al-Dīn, and-said: "My-beloved, until this the-time sitting! Indeed I-said in my-self: to-you and-to-the-groom the-hunchback (is) a-partnership in-me."
sentences.i: When she came into the inner chamber she saw Badr al-Dīn, and said, "My love, still sitting here at this hour? I had said to myself that you and the hunchbacked groom must share a claim on me."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَدْرُ الدِّينِ حَسَنٌ وَأَيْشْ أَوْصَلَ السَّائِسَ إِلَيْكِ وَأَيْنَ لَهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ شَرِيكِي فِيكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla badru al-dīni ḥasanun wa-ayshi awṣala al-sāʾisa ilayki wa-ayna lahu an yakūna sharīkī fīki
sentences.l: And-said Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan: "And-what brought-to the-groom to-you? And-where for-him that he-be my-partner in-you?"
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan said, "What has the groom to do with you? How could he ever be my partner in you?"
sentences.n: وَأَيْشْ is colloquial "what?", a contraction of أَيُّ شَيْءٍ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَمَنْ زَوْجِي أَنْتَ أَوْ هُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat wa-man zawjī anta aw huwa
sentences.l: And-she-said: "And-who (is) my-husband: you or he?"
sentences.i: She said, "Then who is my husband, you or he?"

sentences.t: قَالَ بَدْرُ الدِّينِ يَاسِتَّ الْحُسْنِ نَحْنُ مَا عَمِلْنَا هَٰذَا إِلَّا مَسْخَرَةً لِضَحْكٍ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: qāla badru al-dīni yā-sitta al-ḥusni naḥnu mā ʿamilnā hādhā illā maskharatan li-ḍaḥkin ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Said Badr-al-Dīn: "O Sitt al-Ḥusn, we did-not do this except a-jest, for-laughing at-him."
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn said, "Sitt al-Ḥusn, we did this only as a jest, to laugh at him,"
sentences.n: يَاسِتَّ is printed as one word. This sentence runs straight into the next, which is never completed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتِ الْمَوَاشِطُ وَالْمَغَانِي وَأَهْلُكِ بِجَلْوِكِ عَلَيَّ وَأَنَّ أَبَاكِ اكْتَرَاهُ بِعَشَرَةِ دَنَانِيرَ حَتَّى يَصْرِفَ عَنَّا الْعَيْنَ وَقَدْرَاحَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarati al-mawāshiṭu wa-al-maghānī wa-ahluki bi-jalwiki ʿalayya wa-anna abāki iktarāhu bi-ʿasharati danānīra ḥattā yaṣrifa ʿannā al-ʿayna wa-qadrāḥa
sentences.l: So-when looked the-hairdressers and-the-singing-women and-your-family in-your-displaying upon-me, and-that your-father hired-him for-ten dinars so-that he-turn-away from-us the-eye, and-indeed-he-went.
sentences.i: And when the dressers, the singing-women and your family looked on as you were displayed to me, and your father had hired him for ten dinars to turn the evil eye away from us, he went off.
sentences.n: The sentence is loose: this فَلَمَّا, "when", is never answered, and وَقَدْرَاحَ is printed as one word. The sense seems to be that the dressers, the singing-women and your family all saw you displayed before me, that your father had hired the hunchback for ten dinars as a decoy against the evil eye, and that he has now gone. الْمَغَانِي is read here as "the singing-women"; the form is unusual.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ سِتُّ الْحُسْنِ مِنْ بَدْرِالدِّينِ ذَٰلِكَ الْكَلَامَ تَبَسَّمَتْ وَفَرِحَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat sittu al-ḥusni min badri al-dīni dhālika al-kalāma tabassamat wa-fariḥat
sentences.l: So-when heard Sitt al-Ḥusn from Badr-al-Dīn that the-talk, she-smiled and-rejoiced.
sentences.i: When Sitt al-Ḥusn heard these words from Badr al-Dīn, she smiled and was glad.

sentences.t: وَضَحِكَتْ ضَحْكًا لَطِيفًا وَقَالَتْ وَاللَّٰهِ لَقَدْ أَطْفَأْتَ نَارِي فَبِا للَّٰهِ خُذْنِي إِلَى عِنْدَكَ وَضُمَّنِي إِلَى حِضْنِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ḍaḥikat ḍaḥkan laṭīfan wa-qālat wa-Allāhi laqad aṭfaʾta nārī fa-bi-Allāhi khudhnī ilā ʿindaka wa-ḍummanī ilā ḥiḍnika
sentences.l: And she-laughed a-laugh gentle, and-said: And-by-God, you-have-indeed quenched my-fire! So by-God, take-me to at-you and-press-me to your-bosom.
sentences.i: She laughed a soft laugh and said, "By God, you have put out my fire! So, by God, take me to you and press me to your breast."
sentences.n: The print splits فبالله into فبا and لله; both halves are vocalised as parts of the one oath, "so, by God". The woman is Sitt al-Ḥusn, speaking to her cousin Badr al-Dīn, and "you have put out my fire" is her way of inviting him.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ مِنْ غَيْرِلِبَاسٍ وَكَشَفَتْ ثَوْبَهَا إِلَى رَقَبَتِهَا فَبَانَ كُسُّهَا وَرِدْفُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-kānat min ghayrilibāsin wa-kashafat thawbahā ilā raqabatihā fa-bāna kussuhā wa-ridfuhā
sentences.l: And she-was from without-drawers, and-she-uncovered her-garment up-to her-neck, and-there-appeared her-vulva and-her-rump.
sentences.i: She was wearing no drawers, and she drew her garment up to her neck, and her cunt and her rump lay bare.
sentences.n: غيرلباس is printed as one word. لِبَاس is underwear, drawers (the same garment is سِرْوَال below). ردف is the hindquarters, the rump. The verb فَبَانَ is singular and agrees with the first of its two subjects.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ بَدْرُ الدِّينِ ذَٰلِكَ تَحَرَّكَتْ فِيهِ الشَّهْوَةُ فَقَامَ وَحَلَّ لِبَاسَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara badru al-dīni dhālika taḥarrakat fīhi al-shahwatu fa-qāma wa-ḥalla libāsahu
sentences.l: And-when he-looked, Badr-al-Dīn, at that, there-stirred in-him the-desire; so-he-rose and-undid his-drawers.
sentences.i: When Badr al-Dīn saw that, desire stirred in him, and he got up and untied his drawers.
sentences.n: The name بدرالدين ("full moon of the faith") is printed as one word in most places, and kept so.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْكِيسُ الذَّهَبُ الَّذِي كَانَ أَخَذَهُ مِنَ الْيَهُودِيِّ الَّذِي كَانَ فِيهِ الْأَلْفُ دِينَارٍ لَفَّهُ فِي سِرْوَالِهِ وَحَطَّهُ تَحْتَ ذَيْلِ الطَّرَّاحَةِ وَقَلَعَ شَاشَهُ وَعَلَّقَهَا عَلَى الْكُرْسِيِّ وَبَقِيَ بِالْقَمِيصِ الرَّفِيعِ
sentences.tr: thumma al-kīsu al-dhahabu alladhī kāna akhadhahu min al-yahūdiyyi alladhī kāna fīhi al-alfu dīnārin laffahu fī sirwālihi wa-ḥaṭṭahu taḥta dhayli al-ṭarrāḥati wa-qalaʿa shāshahu wa-ʿallaqahā ʿalā al-kursiyyi wa-baqiya bi-al-qamīṣi al-rafīʿi
sentences.l: Then the-bag, the-gold, which he-had taken-it from the-Jew, which was in-it the-thousand dinar: he-wrapped-it in his-drawers and-put-it under the-edge of-the-mattress; and-he-took-off his-turban-cloth and-hung-it on the-chair, and-remained in-the-shirt the-fine.
sentences.i: Then he wrapped the bag of gold, the one he had taken from the Jew, the one that held the thousand dinars, in his drawers and put it under the edge of the mattress; he took off his turban and hung it on the chair, and stayed in his fine shirt.
sentences.n: The bag is named first and picked up by the pronoun in لَفَّهُ, "he wrapped it"; and الْأَلْفُ دِينَارٍ puts the article on the first word of the phrase, which is how this text usually writes "the thousand dinars". The Jew and his purse come from earlier in the tale. شَاش is a turban-cloth, and the verb "hung" takes it as feminine (عَلَّقَهَا).

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْقَمِيصُ مُطَرَّزًا بِالذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-qamīṣu muṭarrazan bi-al-dhahabi
sentences.l: And the-shirt was embroidered with-the-gold.
sentences.i: The shirt was embroidered with gold.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ قَامَتْ إِلَيْهِ سِتُّ الْحُسْنِ وَجَذَبَتْهُ إِلَيْهَا وَجَذَبَهَا بَدْرُالدِّينِ وَعَانَقَهَا وَأَخَذَ رِجْلَيْهَا فِي وَسَطِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qāmat ilayhi sittu al-ḥusni wa-jadhabathu ilayhā wa-jadhabahā badru al-dīni wa-ʿānaqahā wa-akhadha rijlayhā fī wasaṭihi
sentences.l: And at that, rose to-him Sitt al-Ḥusn, and-drew-him to-her, and-drew-her Badr-al-Dīn, and-embraced-her, and-took her-two-legs in his-middle.
sentences.i: Then Sitt al-Ḥusn rose and went to him and drew him to her, and Badr al-Dīn drew her to him and embraced her and took her legs about his waist.
sentences.n: سِتّ is "lady", the colloquial form of سَيِّدَة; her name means "Lady of Beauty".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَطَّ الذَّخِيرَةَ فَانْطَلَقَ الْمِدْفَعُ هَدَمَ الْبُرْجَ فَوَجَدَهَا دُرَّةً مَا ثُقِبَتْ وَمَطِيَّةً لِغَيْرِهَا مَا رُكِبَتْ فَزَالَ بَكَارَتُهَا وَتَمَلَّى بِشَبَابِهَا ثُمَّ سَلَّهُ مِنْهَا وَرَدَّنَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥaṭṭa al-dhakhīrata fa-inṭalaqa al-midfaʿu hadama al-burja fa-wajadahā durratan mā thuqibat wa-maṭiyyatan li-ghayrihā mā rukibat fa-zāla bakāratuhā wa-tamallā bi-shabābihā thumma sallahu minhā wa-radda-nahu
sentences.l: Then he-set the-ammunition, and-went-off the-cannon, it-demolished the-tower; and-he-found-her a-pearl not pierced, and-a-mount for other-than-her not ridden; and-went her-virginity, and-he-took-his-fill of-her youth; then he-drew-it from-her and-put-back-(?)-it.
sentences.i: Then he loaded the charge, and the cannon went off and brought down the tower. He found her a pearl unpierced, a mount that no one else had ridden. Her maidenhead was gone, and he took his fill of her youth; then he drew out of her and put it back in.
sentences.n: The cannon, the charge and the tower are the text's own figure for the act; سَلَّهُ, "he drew it out", is the word for drawing a sword. لِغَيْرِهَا مَا رُكِبَتْ: "for anyone but her", the li- naming the rider, so "ridden for no other". The last word وَرَدَّنَهُ is obscure: the sense is surely "and put it back" (وَرَدَّهُ), but the print has an extra ن that I cannot explain, and I have pointed the letters as printed. The verb فَزَالَ is masculine because it comes before its subject.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ أَعَادَهُ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ مَرَّةً فَعَلِقَتْ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha aʿādahu khamsata ʿashara marratan fa-ʿaliqat minhu
sentences.l: And-when he-finished, he-returned-it fifteen times; and-she-conceived from-him.
sentences.i: When he had finished, he did it again, fifteen times in all, and she conceived by him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ وَضَعَ يَدَهُ تَحْتَ رَأْسِهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ الْأُخْرَيٰ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا تَعَانَقَا وَنَامَا مُتَعَانِقَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha badru al-dīni waḍaʿa yadahu taḥta raʾsihā wa-kadhālika al-ukhrā thumma innahumā taʿānaqā wa-nāmā mutaʿāniqayni
sentences.l: And-when he-finished, Badr-al-Dīn, he-placed his-hand under her-head, and-likewise the-other; then, they-two embraced and-slept embracing.
sentences.i: When Badr al-Dīn had finished, he put one hand under her head, and the other likewise; then the two embraced and fell asleep in each other's arms.
sentences.n: الأخرى is printed with a final ي rather than ى; it is read -ā, and the dagger alif is ours.

sentences.t: كَمَا قَالَ فِيهِمَا الشَّاعِرُ هَٰذِهِ الْأَ بْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: kamā qāla fīhimā al-shāʿiru hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: As said of-them-two the-poet these the-verses:
sentences.i: as the poet said of them in these lines:
sentences.n: The print breaks الأبيات into الأ and بيات; they are read together.

sentences.t:
زُرْ مَنْ تُحِبُّ وَدَعْ كَلَامَ الْحَاسِدِ * لَيْسَ الْحَسُودُ عَلَى الْهَوَى بِمُسَاعِدِ
لَنْ يَخْلُقَ الرَّحْمَنُ اَحْسَنَ مَنْظِرًا * مِنْ عَاشِقَيْنِ عَلَى فِرَاشٍ وَاحِدِ
مُتَعَانِقَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا حُلَلُ الرِّضَا * مُتَوَسِّدَيْنِ بِمِعْصَمٍ وَبِسَاعِدِ
وَاِذَا تَاَلَّفَتِ الْقُلُوبُ مَعَ الْهَوَى * فَالنَّاسُ تَضْرِبُ فِي حَدِيدٍ بَارِدِ
وَاِذَا صَفَالَكَ مِنْ زَمَانِكَ وَاحِدٌ * نِعْمَ الصَّدِيقُ وَعِشْ بِذَاكَ الْوَاحِدِ
يَامَنْ يَلُومُ عَلَى الْهَوَى اَهْلَ الْهَوَى * هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ صَلَاحَ قَلْبٍ فَاسِدِ
sentences.tr:
zur man tuḥibbu wa-daʿ kalāma al-ḥāsidi * laysa al-ḥasūdu ʿalā al-hawā bi-musāʿidi
lan yakhluqa al-raḥmānu aḥsana manẓaran * min ʿāshiqayni ʿalā firāshin wāḥidi
mutaʿāniqayni ʿalayhimā ḥulalu al-riḍā * mutawassidayni bi-miʿṣamin wa-bi-sāʿidi
wa-idhā taʾallafati al-qulūbu maʿa al-hawā * fa-al-nāsu taḍribu fī ḥadīdin bāridi
wa-idhā ṣafā laka min zamānika wāḥidun * niʿma al-ṣadīqu wa-ʿish bi-dhāka al-wāḥidi
yā man yalūmu ʿalā al-hawā ahla al-hawā * hal yastaṭīʿu ṣalāḥa qalbin fāsidi
sentences.l:
Visit whom you-love and-leave the-speech of-the-envier, * not-is the-envious in the-love a-helper;
Never will-create the-All-Merciful a-fairer sight * than two-lovers on a-bed one,
Two-embracing, upon-them-two the-robes of-contentment, * two-pillowed on-a-wrist and-on-a-forearm.
And-when are-joined the-hearts with the-love, * then the-people strike on iron cold.
And-when is-pure for-you from your-time one, * excellent the-friend! and-live with that the-one.
O who blames, for the-love, the-people-of the-love, * can he-be-able the-mending of-a-heart corrupt?
sentences.i: Visit the one you love and leave the talk of the envier; the envious man is no helper in love. The All-Merciful will never create a fairer sight than two lovers on one bed, embracing, robes of contentment upon them, their heads pillowed on wrist and forearm. When hearts are joined in love, people are beating cold iron. And if one in your whole age is true to you, an excellent friend, then live by that one. You who blame the people of love for love: can he mend a corrupt heart?
sentences.n: The edition points its verse and the pointing is kept as printed. اَحْسَنَ, وَاِذَا and اَهْلَ are written with a plain alif carrying the vowel sign, as in the print. يَامَنْ (يَا مَنْ) and صَفَالَكَ (صَفَا لَكَ) are printed as one word each. The final -i of وَاحِدِ, بَارِدِ, فَاسِدِ and the like is the rhyme vowel; the nunation is dropped for the metre. حَدِيدٍ بَارِدِ, "cold iron", is what one beats to no purpose: where hearts are joined, whoever tries to part them toils for nothing. تَضْرِبُ has a feminine verb with النَّاسُ, a collective.

sentences.t: هَٰذَ امَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ وَسِتِّ الْحُسْنِ بِنْتِ عَمِّهِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri badri al-dīni ḥasanin wa-sitti al-ḥusni binti ʿammihi
sentences.l: This, what was of the-matter of-Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan and-Sitt al-Ḥusn, daughter of-his-paternal-uncle;
sentences.i: So much for what befell Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan and Sitt al-Ḥusn, his cousin.
sentences.n: The print writes هذ اما, with the alif of هذا slipped onto the next word; read هَذَا مَا. مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ فُلَان, "what was of the affair of so-and-so", is the storyteller's formula for "what happened to him", and it turns the tale to another thread, as in the next sentence. بِنْتُ عَمِّهِ, "daughter of his paternal uncle", is his cousin.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْعِفْرِيتِ فَإِنَّهُ قَالَ لِلْعِفْرِيتَةِ قُومِي وَادْخُلِي تَحْتَ الشَّابِّ وَدَعِينَا نُوَدِّيهِ مَكَانَهُ لِئَلَّا يُدْرِكَنَا الصُّبْحُ لِأَنَّ الْوَقْتَ قَرِيبٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-ʿifrīti fa-innahu qāla li-al-ʿifrītati qūmī wa-udkhulī taḥta al-shābbi wa-daʿīnā nuwaddīhi makānahu li-allā yudrikanā al-ṣubḥu li-anna al-waqta qarībun
sentences.l: And as-for what was of the-matter of-the-ifrit, indeed-he said to-the-she-ifrit: Rise and-enter under the-youth, and-leave-us we-convey-him to-his-place, lest overtake-us the-morning, for the-time is-near.
sentences.i: As for what happened with the ifrit, he said to the she-ifrit, "Get up and go in under the youth, and let us carry him to his place before the morning overtakes us, for the time is near."
sentences.n: The ifrit is a mighty jinni and the she-ifrit his female counterpart; they have just carried Sitt al-Ḥusn's cousin out of her bed. دَعِينَا نُوَدِّيهِ, "leave us, we convey him", has no أَنْ before the second verb, an everyday construction. نُوَدِّيهِ is spelled with و, so the pointing follows the letters; it is the verb "to deliver" (أَدَّى, in the colloquial form waddā).

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ تَقَدَّمَتِ الْعِفْرِيتَةُ وَدَخَلَتْ تَحْتَ ذَيْلِهِ وَهُوَ نَائِمٌ وَأَخَذَتْهُ وَطَارَتْ بِهِ وَهُوَ عَلَى حَالِهِ بِالْقَمِيصِ وَهُوَ بِلَا لِبَاسٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqaddamati al-ʿifrītatu wa-dakhalat taḥta dhaylihi wa-huwa nāʾimun wa-akhadhat-hu wa-ṭārat bihi wa-huwa ʿalā ḥālihi bi-al-qamīṣi wa-huwa bi-lā libāsin
sentences.l: And at that, advanced the-she-ifrit and-entered under his-hem while-he asleep, and-took-him and-flew with-him, while-he on his-state in-the-shirt, and-he without drawers.
sentences.i: Then the she-ifrit stepped forward and slipped in under his skirts as he slept, and took him up and flew off with him, just as he was, in his shirt and without drawers.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَتِ الْعِفْرِيتَةُ طَايِرَةً بِهِ وَالْعِفْرِيتُ يُحَاذِيهَا فَأَدْرَكَهُمُ الصَّبَاحُ فِي أَثْنَاءِ الطَّرِيقِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālati al-ʿifrītatu ṭāyiratan bihi wa-al-ʿifrītu yuḥādhīhā fa-adrakahumu al-ṣabāḥu fī athnāʾi al-ṭarīqi
sentences.l: And not ceased the-she-ifrit flying with-him, and-the-ifrit keeping-abreast-of-her, and-overtook-them the-morning amid the-folds of-the-road.
sentences.i: The she-ifrit kept flying with him, and the ifrit kept alongside her, and morning overtook them in the midst of the journey.
sentences.n: طَايِرَةً is the print's spelling of طَائِرَةً, "flying", with ي for the hamza; it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَ الْمُؤَذِّنُونَ بِحَيَّ عَلَى الْفَلَاحِ فَأَذِنَ اللَّٰهُ مَلَايِكَتَهُ أَنْ تَرْمِيَ الْعِفْرِيتَ بِشُهُبٍ مِنْ نَارٍ فَاحْتَرَقَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥa al-muʾadhdhinūna bi-ḥayya ʿalā al-falāḥi fa-adhina Allāhu malāyikatahu an tarmiya al-ʿifrīta bi-shuhubin min nārin fa-iḥtaraqa
sentences.l: And-cried the-muezzins with "Hasten to the-success"; and-permitted God his-angels that they-cast the-ifrit with-flames of fire; and-he-burned-up.
sentences.i: The muezzins cried out, "Come to salvation!", and God gave his angels leave to pelt the ifrit with shooting flames of fire, and he burned up.
sentences.n: حَيَّ عَلَى الْفَلَاحِ is a phrase of the call to prayer, quoted. فَأَذِنَ with a direct object (مَلَايِكَتَهُ) is unusual, since أَذِنَ normally takes لِـ; the consonants would also allow فَآذَنَ, "he gave notice to", and the sense is much the same. The ifrit is struck by shooting stars, the traditional punishment of jinn who climb toward heaven. مَلَايِكَة is the print's spelling of مَلَائِكَة.

sentences.t: وَسَلِمَتِ الْعِفْرِيتَةُ فَنَزَلَتْ بِبَدْرِالدِّينِ فِي مَوْضِعٍ مَا أَخَذَتِ الشُّهُبُ الْعِفْرِيتَ وَلَمْ تَتَعَدَّ بِهِ خَوْفًا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-salimati al-ʿifrītatu fa-nazalat bi-badri al-dīni fī mawḍiʿin mā akhadhati al-shuhubu al-ʿifrīta wa-lam tataʿadda bihi khawfan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-was-safe the-she-ifrit, and-descended with-Badr-al-Dīn in-a-place that took the-flames the-ifrit, and-did-not go-beyond with-him, in-fear for-him.
sentences.i: The she-ifrit escaped unharmed and came down with Badr al-Dīn at the place where the flames had struck the ifrit, and did not carry him on, for fear of what might happen to him.
sentences.n: مَا before the verb is the awkward word here. I read it as a relative ("a place where the flames took the ifrit"), so that she lands at once and dares not fly farther; a negative ("a place the flames had not taken the ifrit in") is possible but gives a worse sense. The verb of أَخَذَتِ is feminine with the plural الشُّهُب, as is usual with a plural of things.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرِ قَدْ وَصَلُوا دِمَشْقَ الشَّامِ فَوَضَعَتْهُ الْعِفْرِيتَةُ عَلَى بَابٍ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا وَطَارَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna bi-al-amri al-muqaddari qad waṣalū dimashqa al-shāmi fa-waḍaʿat-hu al-ʿifrītatu ʿalā bābin min abwābihā wa-ṭārat
sentences.l: And-it-was by-the-matter the-decreed (that) they-had arrived (at) Damascus of-Syria; and-set-him the-she-ifrit on a-gate of her-gates, and-flew-off.
sentences.i: By decree of fate they had come as far as Damascus in Syria; the she-ifrit set him down at one of its gates and flew away.
sentences.n: وَكَانَ بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرِ قَدْ وَصَلُوا: "it was, by the ordained matter, that they had arrived", a loose construction in which the arrival is the thing that was ordained.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَلَعَ النَّهَارُ وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُ الْمَدِينَةِ وَخَرَجَ النَّاسُ فَنَظَرُوا شَابًّا مَلِيحًا بِقَمِيصٍ وَطَاقِيَةٍ كُشِفَ مِنْ غَيْرِ لِبَاسٍ وَهُوَ مِمَّا قَاسَى مِنَ السَّهَرِ غَرْقَانُ فِي النَّوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭalaʿa al-nahāru wa-futiḥat abwābu al-madīnati wa-kharaja al-nāsu fa-naẓarū shābban malīḥan bi-qamīṣin wa-ṭāqiyatin kushifa min ghayri libāsin wa-huwa mimmā qāsā min al-sahari gharqānu fī al-nawmi
sentences.l: And-when rose the-day, and-were-opened the-gates of-the-city, and-went-out the-people, they-looked (at) a-youth handsome, in-a-shirt and-a-cap, bared from without-drawers, and-he, from-what he-suffered of-the-wakefulness, drowned in the-sleep.
sentences.i: At sunrise, when the gates of the city were opened and the people went out, they saw a handsome young man in a shirt and a skullcap, stripped bare of any drawers, and, worn out by the sleepless night, sunk in sleep.
sentences.n: كُشِفَ is read as a passive verb, "he had been bared", used as a description of the youth. The print gives only كشف, and other readings of it are possible. طَاقِيَة is a skullcap. غَرْقَانُ فِي النَّوْمِ, "drowned in sleep", is a common figure for a very deep sleeper.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ النَّاسُ قَالُوا يَا بَخْتَ مَنْ كَانَ هَٰذَا عِنْدَهُ اللَّيْلَةَ وَيَا لَيْتَهُ صَبَرَ حَتَّى لَبِسَ حَوَائِجَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾawhu al-nāsu qālū yā bakhta man kāna hādhā ʿindahu al-laylata wa-yā laytahu ṣabara ḥattā labisa ḥawāʾijahu
sentences.l: And-when they-saw-him the-people, they-said: O luck of-him-who was this with-him tonight! And-O would-that-he had-waited until he-put-on his-things!
sentences.i: When the people saw him they said, "How lucky is the man who had this one with him tonight! If only he had waited until he put on his clothes!"
sentences.n: رَاَوْهُ النَّاسُ has a plural verb before its plural subject, where Classical Arabic would use the singular; this is common in Middle Arabic and is kept as printed. The people take him for someone's lover of the night before. حَوَائِج is "needs" in Classical Arabic and, as here, "belongings, clothes" in the colloquial.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ مِسْكِينٌ أُولَادُ النَّاسِ هَٰذِهِ السَّاعَةَ خَرَجَ مِنَ الْخَمَّارَةِ لِبَعْضِ شُغْلِهِ فَقَوِيَ عَلَيْهِ السُّكْرُ فَتَاهَ عَنِ الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي كَانَ قَاصِدَهُ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى بَابِ الْمَدِينَةِ فَوَجَدَهُ مَغْلُوقًا فَنَامَ هُنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-ākharu miskīnun awlādu al-nāsi hādhihi al-sāʿata kharaja min al-khammārati li-baʿḍi shughlihi fa-qawiya ʿalayhi al-sukru fa-tāha ʿan al-makāni alladhī kāna qāṣidahu ḥattā waṣala ilā bābi al-madīnati fa-wajadahu maghlūqan fa-nāma hunā
sentences.l: And-said the-other: A-poor-one, the-sons of-the-people! This hour he-went-out from the-wine-shop for some of-his-business, and-grew-strong upon-him the-drunkenness, and-he-lost-his-way from the-place which he-was heading-for-it, until he-reached to the-gate of-the-city, and-found-it locked, and-slept here.
sentences.i: Another said, "Poor fellow, a gentleman's son! He left the tavern just now on some errand of his, and the wine overcame him, and he lost his way from the place he was making for, until he reached the city gate, found it shut, and lay down to sleep here."
sentences.n: أُولَادُ النَّاسِ, "the sons of the people", means people of good family. مَغْلُوقًا is the colloquial "locked" (the Classical participle is مُغْلَق).

sentences.t: وَقَدْ خَاضَ النَّاسُ فِيهِ بِالْكَلَامِ وَإِذَا بِالْهَوَاءِ هَبَّ عَلَى بَدْرِالدِّينِ رَفَعَ ذَيْلَهُ إِلَى بَطْنِهِ فَبَانَ مِنْ تَحْتِهِ بَطْنٌ وَسُرَّةٌ مُحَقَّقَةٌ وَسِيقَانٌ وَأَفْخَاذٌ مِثْلُ الْبَلُّورِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad khāḍa al-nāsu fīhi bi-al-kalāmi wa-idhā bi-al-hawāʾi habba ʿalā badri al-dīni rafaʿa dhaylahu ilā baṭnihi fa-bāna min taḥtihi baṭnun wa-surratun muḥaqqaqatun wa-sīqānun wa-afkhādhun mithlu al-ballūri
sentences.l: And the-people had plunged in-him in-talk; and-behold, with-the-wind it-blew on Badr-al-Dīn, it-lifted his-hem to his-belly, and-there-appeared from beneath-him a-belly and-a-navel well-formed, and-shins and-thighs like the-crystal.
sentences.i: The people had been talking about him when suddenly a wind blew on Badr al-Dīn and lifted his hem to his belly, and there showed beneath it a belly and a shapely navel, and shins and thighs like crystal.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِالْهَوَاءِ هَبَّ: after إِذَا of surprise the بِـ only marks what appears, "and behold, a wind"; the verb that follows (هَبَّ, then رَفَعَ) simply tells what it did. مُحَقَّقَة is "well-formed, exact"; the word is not wholly certain.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ النَّاسُ وَاللَّٰهِ طَيِّبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-nāsu wa-Allāhi ṭayyibun
sentences.l: And-said the-people: By-God, good!
sentences.i: And the people said, "By God, how fine!"
sentences.n: طَيِّب here is a colloquial exclamation of approval, "good!".

sentences.t: فَانْتَبَهَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ فَوَجَدَ رُوحَهُ عَلَى بَابِ مَدِينَةٍ وَعَلَيْهَا نَاسٌ فَتَعَجَّبَ وَ قَالَ أَنَافَيْن يَا جَمَاعَةَ الْخَيْرِ وَمَا سَبَبُ اجْتِمَاعِكُمْ وَمَا حِكَايَتِي مَعَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-intabaha badru al-dīni fa-wajada rūḥahu ʿalā bābi madīnatin wa-ʿalayhā nāsun fa-taʿajjaba wa-qāla anā-fayn yā jamāʿata al-khayri wa-mā sababu ijtimāʿikum wa-mā ḥikāyatī maʿakum
sentences.l: And-he-awoke, Badr-al-Dīn, and-found his-spirit at a-gate of-a-city and-upon-it people; and-he-marvelled, and said: I-am-where, O company of-the-good? And-what the-cause of-your-gathering, and-what my-tale with-you?
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn woke and found himself at the gate of a city, with people about him; he marvelled, and said, "Where am I, good people? What is the reason for your gathering, and what have I to do with you?"
sentences.n: رُوحَهُ is "his spirit" used for "himself", as in the colloquial. The print breaks وقال after its و, at the end of a line; the two pieces are kept apart. أَنَافَيْن, printed as one word, is colloquial "anā fēn", "where am I", with فَيْن from فِي + أَيْن. حِكَايَتِي مَعَكُمْ, "my story with you", is "what business have I with you".

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا نَحْنُ رَأَيْنَاكَ عِنْدَ أَذَانِ الصُّبْحِ مُلْقًى نَائِمًا وَلَا نَعْلَمُ مِنْ أَمْرٍ غَيْرِ هَٰذَا فَأَيْنَ كُنْتَ نَائِمًا هَٰذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū naḥnu raʾaynāka ʿinda adhāni al-ṣubḥi mulqan nāʾiman wa-lā naʿlamu min amrin ghayri hādhā fa-ayna kunta nāʾiman hādhihi al-laylata
sentences.l: And-they-said: We, we-saw-you at the-call of-the-morning thrown-down asleep, and-we-do-not know of any-matter other-than this. So where were-you sleeping this night?
sentences.i: They said, "We saw you at the morning call to prayer, lying here asleep, and we know nothing more than that. So where were you sleeping last night?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ وَاللَّٰهِ يَا جَمَاعَةُ كُنْتُ نَائِمًا هَٰذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ فِي مِصْرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla badru al-dīni ḥasanun wa-Allāhi yā jamāʿatu kuntu nāʾiman hādhihi al-laylata fī miṣra
sentences.l: So-said Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan: By-God, O company, I-was sleeping this night in Egypt.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan said, "By God, good people, last night I was sleeping in Egypt."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاحِدٌ أَنْتَ تَأْكُلُ حَشِيش
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wāḥidun anta taʾkulu ḥashīsh
sentences.l: And-said one: You, you-eat hashish.
sentences.i: One said, "You've been eating hashish!"
sentences.n: حَشِيش is left without a case ending. It is the object, and Classical Arabic would write حَشِيشًا, but the print gives no alif and so no tanwīn can be shown.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَنْتَ مَجْنُونٌ تَكُونُ بَائِتًا فِي مِصْرَ وَتُصْبِحُ نَائِمًا فِي مَدِينَةِ دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla baʿḍuhum anta majnūnun takūnu bāʾitan fī miṣra wa-tuṣbiḥu nāʾiman fī madīnati dimashqa
sentences.l: And-said some-of-them: You are-mad! You-are spending-the-night in Egypt and-you-come-to-morning sleeping in the-city of-Damascus!
sentences.i: Others said, "You are mad! You spend the night in Egypt and wake up asleep in the city of Damascus?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ وَاللَّٰهِ يَا جَمَاعَةَ الْخَيْرِ لَمْ أَكْذِبْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَبَدًا وَأَنَا كُنْتُ الْبَارِحَةَ بِاللَّيْلِ فِي دِيَارِ مِصْرَ وَفِى النَّهَارِ أَمْسِ كُنْتُ بِالْبَصْرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum wa-Allāhi yā jamāʿata al-khayri lam akdhib ʿalaykum abadan wa-anā kuntu al-bāriḥata bi-al-layli fī diyāri miṣra wa-fī al-nahāri amsi kuntu bi-al-baṣrati
sentences.l: So-he-said to-them: By-God, O company of-the-good, I-have-not lied to-you ever; and-I, I-was last-night by-the-night in the-lands of-Egypt, and-in the-day yesterday I-was in-Baṣra.
sentences.i: He said to them, "By God, good people, I have never lied to you. Last night I was in the land of Egypt, and yesterday, in the daytime, I was in Basra."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاحِدٌ طَيِّبٌ وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ هَٰذَا الشَّابُّ مَجْنُونٌ وَصَفَّقُوا عَلَيْهِ بِالْكُفُوفِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wāḥidun ṭayyibun wa-qāla al-ākharu hādhā al-shābbu majnūnun wa-ṣaffaqū ʿalayhi bi-al-kufūfi
sentences.l: And-said one: Good! And-said the-other: This the-youth is-mad. And-they-clapped at-him with-the-palms.
sentences.i: One said, "Fine!" and another said, "This young man is mad," and they clapped their hands at him.

sentences.t: وَتَحَدَّثَتِ النَّاسُ بَعْضُهُمْ مَعَ بَعْضٍ وَقَالُوا يَا خَسَارَةَ شَبَابِهِ وَاللَّٰهِ مَانِي جُنُونِهِ شَكٌّ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: wa-taḥaddathati al-nāsu baʿḍuhum maʿa baʿḍin wa-qālū yā khasārata shabābihi wa-Allāhi mānī junūnihi shakkun abadan
sentences.l: And-talked the-people, some-of-them with others, and-they-said: O the-loss of-his-youth! By-God, (there-is-)not of-his-madness doubt ever.
sentences.i: The people talked among themselves and said, "What a waste of his youth! By God, there is no doubt of his madness at all."
sentences.n: تَحَدَّثَتِ النَّاسُ has a feminine singular verb with النَّاس, a collective; a feminine singular is normal for a collective in Middle Arabic. مَانِي is obscure: the sense must be "there is no", and I take it as a spelling of مَا فِي, with the vowel of فِي kept in the following جُنُونِهِ. Another possibility is the colloquial "mānī", "I am not", with the clause then running "I am not (in) doubt of his madness".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ قَالُوا لَهُ دَبِّرْ بَالَكَ وَارْجِعْ لِعَقْلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum qālū lahu dabbir bālaka wa-arjiʿ li-ʿaqlika
sentences.l: Then, they said to-him: Manage your-mind, and-return to-your-reason.
sentences.i: Then they said to him, "Mind yourself, and come back to your senses."
sentences.n: دَبِّرْ بَالَكَ, "manage your mind", is the colloquial "take care, pull yourself together".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ كُنْتُ الْبَارِحَةَ عَرِس فِي دِيَارِ مِصْرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla badru al-dīni ḥasanun kuntu al-bāriḥata ʿarīs fī diyāri miṣra
sentences.l: So-said Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan: I-was last-night a-bridegroom in the-lands of-Egypt.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan said, "Last night I was a bridegroom in the land of Egypt."
sentences.n: The print has عرس without the long vowel. I read it as عَرِيس, "bridegroom", and point only the letters that are there; the alternative is عُرْس, "wedding", but "I was a wedding" does not work.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَعَلَّكَ حَلَمْتَ وَرَأَيْتَ هَٰذَا الَّذِي تَقُولُ فِي الْمَنَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū laʿallaka ḥalamta wa-raʾayta hādhā alladhī taqūlu fī al-manāmi
sentences.l: And-they-said: Perhaps-you dreamed, and-saw this which you-say in the-sleep.
sentences.i: They said, "Perhaps you were dreaming, and saw in your sleep what you are telling us."

sentences.t: فَتَوَهَّمَ حَسَنٌ فِي نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-tawahhama ḥasanun fī nafsihi
sentences.l: And-supposed Ḥasan in his-self.
sentences.i: Ḥasan turned it over in his mind.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُمْ وَاللَّٰهِ مَا هَٰذَا مَنَامٌ وَلَا رَأَيْتُهُ فِى الْأَحْلَامِ إِلَّا إِنِّي رُحْتُ وَقَدْ جَلَوُا الْعَرُوسَةَ قُدَّامِي وَكَانَ الثَّالِثُ الْأَ حْدَبُ قَاعِدًا وَاللَّٰهِ يَا أَخِي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahum wa-Allāhi mā hādhā manāmun wa-lā raʾaytuhu fī al-aḥlāmi illā innī ruḥtu wa-qad jalawā al-ʿarūsata quddāmī wa-kāna al-thālithu al-aḥdabu qāʿidan wa-Allāhi yā akhī
sentences.l: And-he-said to-them: By-God, not this is a-dream, and-not did-I-see-it in the-dreams; except that-I went, and they-had-displayed the-bride before-me; and-was the-third, the-hunchback, sitting. By-God, O my-brother
sentences.i: He said to them, "By God, this is no dream, and I never saw it in dreams. No: I went, and they had paraded the bride before me; and the third, the hunchback, was sitting there. By God, my brother,"
sentences.n: قُدَّامِي is colloquial "in front of me". جَلَوُا الْعَرُوسَةَ is the technical phrase for displaying the bride to the groom. الثَّالِثُ الْأَحْدَبُ is printed with the article split from the noun (الا حدب); "the third" refers to a company named before this passage.

sentences.t: مَا هَذَا مَنَامٌ وَلَوْكَانَ مَنَامًا أَيْنَ كَانَ الْكِيسُ الذَّهَبُ مَعِي وَأَيْنَ شَاشِي وَثِيَابِي وَلِبَاسِي
sentences.tr: mā hādhā manāmun wa-law-kāna manāman ayna kāna al-kīsu al-dhahabu maʿī wa-ayna shāshī wa-thiyābī wa-libāsī
sentences.l: Not this a-dream; and-if-it-were a-dream, where was the-purse the-gold with-me, and-where my-turban and-my-clothes and-my-garment?
sentences.i: This is no dream; and if it were a dream, where would the purse of gold be that was with me, and where my turban, my clothes and my robe?
sentences.n: الْكِيسُ الذَّهَبُ puts two definite nouns side by side, “the purse the gold”, where Classical would say كِيسُ الذَّهَبِ, “the purse of gold”. Middle Arabic uses this kind of apposition freely.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَ وَدَخَلَ الْمَدِينَةَ وَشَقَّ شَوَارِعَهَا وَأَسْوَاقَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma qāma wa-dakhala al-madīnata wa-shaqqa shawāriʿahā wa-aswāqahā
sentences.l: Then he-rose and-entered the-city and-cleft its-streets and-its-markets.
sentences.i: Then he got up and entered the city, making his way through its streets and its markets.

sentences.t: فَازْدَحَمَتِ النَّاسُ عَلَيْهِ وَزَفُّوهُ فَدَخَلَ دُكَّانَ طَبَّاخٍ
sentences.tr: fa-izdaḥamati al-nāsu ʿalayhi wa-zaffūhu fa-dakhala dukkāna ṭabbākhin
sentences.l: So-crowded (f.) the-people upon-him, and-they-led-him-in-procession, so-he-entered a-shop-of a-cook.
sentences.i: The people crowded round him and led him along in procession, and he went into a cook's shop.
sentences.n: ازْدَحَمَتِ is feminine singular before the collective النَّاسُ, “the people”, a common Middle Arabic agreement. زَفَّ is the verb for conducting a bride in procession; here the crowd escorts him noisily along.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ الطَّبَّاخُ رَجُلًا شَاطِرًا يَعْنِي حَرَامِيًّا فَتَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحَرَامِ وَفَتَحَ لَهُ دُكَّانَ طَبَّاخٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna dhālika al-ṭabbākhu rajulan shāṭiran yaʿnī ḥarāmiyyan fa-tāba Allāhu ʿalayhi min al-ḥarāmi wa-fataḥa lahu dukkāna ṭabbākhin
sentences.l: And-was that the-cook a-man a-rogue, meaning a-thief; so-turned God upon-him from the-forbidden, and-opened for-him a-shop-of a-cook.
sentences.i: Now this cook had been a rogue, that is, a thief, until God accepted his repentance from the unlawful, and opened for him a cook's shop.
sentences.n: شَاطِر is a clever, bold fellow, often a ruffian; the narrator glosses it for his reader with the colloquial حَرَامِيّ, “thief” (from حَرَام, “forbidden”). تَابَ عَلَيْهِ, “turned upon him”, is said of God accepting a sinner's repentance. The shop is presumably God's gift in the sense of a livelihood made lawful.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَهْلُ دِمَشْقَ كُلُّهُمْ يَخَافُونَ مِنْهُ وَمِنْ شِدَّةِ بَأْسِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ahlu dimashqa kulluhum yakhāfūna minhu wa-min shiddati baʾsihi
sentences.l: And-were the-people-of Damascus, all-of-them, fearing from-him and-from the-severity-of his-might.
sentences.i: And all the people of Damascus feared him, and feared the fierceness of his strength.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ النَّاسُ إِلَى الشَّابِّ وَقَدْ دَخَلَ دُكَّانَ الطَّبَّاخِ افْتَرَقُوا وَخَافُوا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara al-nāsu ilā al-shābbi wa-qad dakhala dukkāna al-ṭabbākhi iftaraqū wa-khāfū minhu
sentences.l: So-when looked the-people at the-youth, and-he-had entered the-shop-of the-cook, they-dispersed and-feared from-him.
sentences.i: When the people saw the young man go into the cook's shop, they scattered, afraid of the cook.
sentences.n: The مِنْهُ at the end is the cook.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ طَبَّاخٌ إِلَى بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى حُسْنِهِ وَجَمَالِهِ وَقَعَتْ فِي قَلْبِهِ مَحَبَّةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara ṭabbākhun ilā badri al-dīni ḥasanin wa-naẓara ilā ḥusnihi wa-jamālihi waqaʿat fī qalbihi maḥabbatun
sentences.l: So-when looked a-cook at Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan, and-looked at his-beauty and-his-comeliness, there-fell in his-heart a-love.
sentences.i: When the cook looked at Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and looked upon his beauty and his comeliness, love for him fell into the cook's heart.
sentences.n: طَبَّاخٌ is printed without the article, “a cook” for “the cook”; it is the same man. Names ending in الدِّين are printed in one word here, بَدْرِالدِّينِ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ يَافَتَى فَا حْكِ لِي حِكَايَتَكَ فَإِنَّكَ صِرْتَ عِنْدِي أَعَزَّ مِنْ رُوحِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu min ayna anta yā-fatā fa-ḥkī lī ḥikāyataka fa-innaka ṣirta ʿindī aʿazza min rūḥī
sentences.l: So-he-said to-him: From where are-you, O-youth? So tell to-me your-tale, for-you have-become with-me dearer than my-soul.
sentences.i: He said to him, “Where are you from, young man? Tell me your story, for you have become dearer to me than my own life.”
sentences.n: The print splits فَا from حْكِ. The alif is the helping alif of the imperative اِحْكِ, which is silent after فَـ; read fa-ḥkī, “so tell”.

sentences.t: فَحَكَى لَهُ مَا جَرَى مِنَ الْمُبْتَدَا إِلَى الْمُنْتَهَى
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakā lahu mā jarā min al-mubtadā ilā al-muntahā
sentences.l: So-he-related to-him what happened from the-beginning to the-end.
sentences.i: So he told him all that had happened, from beginning to end.
sentences.n: الْمُبْتَدَا is printed with a final alif where Classical writes ى (الْمُبْتَدَى).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الطَّبَّاخُ يَا سَيِّدِي بَدْرَالدِّينِ اِعْلَمْ أَنَّ هَذَا أَمْرٌ عَجِيبٌ وَحَدِيثٌ غَرِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-ṭabbākhu yā sayyidī badra al-dīni iʿlam anna hādhā amrun ʿajībun wa-ḥadīthun gharībun
sentences.l: So-said to-him the-cook: O my-lord Badr-al-Dīn, know that this a-matter wondrous and-a-report strange.
sentences.i: The cook said to him, “My lord Badr al-Dīn, know that this is a marvellous matter and a strange tale.”
sentences.n: عَجِيبٌ and غَرِيبٌ rhyme, as often in these formal speeches.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ يَا وَلَدِي اُكْتُمْ مَا مَعَكَ حَتَّى يُفَرِّجَ اللَّهُ مَابِكَ وَاقْعُدْ عِنْدِي فِي هَذَا الْمَكَانِ وَإِنَّ مَالِي وَلَدٌ وَأَتَّخِذُكَ وَلَدِي
sentences.tr: wa-lākin yā waladī uktum mā maʿaka ḥattā yufarrija Allāhu mābika wa-uqʿud ʿindī fī hādhā al-makāni wa-inna mālī waladun wa-attakhidhuka waladī
sentences.l: But O my-child, conceal what is-with-you until God eases what-is-with-you; and-sit with-me in this the-place; for not-to-me a-child, and-I-take-you my-child.
sentences.i: But, my son, keep to yourself what you have with you, until God relieves your trouble; and stay with me in this place, for I have no son, and I will take you as my own son.
sentences.n: مَابِكَ is مَا بِكَ run together, “what is with you”, that is, what ails you. مَالِي وَلَدٌ is “I have no child” (literally “what is to me, a child?”). I read وَاتَّخِذُكَ as a first-person imperfect, “and I take you as”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ بَدْرُ الدِّينِ نَعَمْ يَاعَمِّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu badru al-dīni naʿam yā-ʿammi
sentences.l: So-said to-him Badr al-Dīn: Yes, O-paternal-uncle.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn said to him, “Yes, uncle.”
sentences.n: عَمّ, a father's brother, is also the polite address to an older man.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَزَلَ الطَّبَّاخُ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَاشْتَرَى لِبَدْرِالدِّينِ أَقْمِشَةً مُفْتَخِرَةً وَأَلْبَسَهَا لَهُ وَتَوَجَّهَ وَإِيَّاهُ إِلَى الْقَاضِي وَأَشْهَرَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَنَّهُ وَلَدُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika nazala al-ṭabbākhu ilā al-sūqi wa-ishtarā li-badri al-dīni aqmishatan muftakhiratan wa-albasahā lahu wa-tawajjaha wa-iyyāhu ilā al-qāḍī wa-ashhara ʿalā nafsihi annahu waladuhu
sentences.l: So at that went-down the-cook to the-market, and-bought for-Badr-al-Dīn cloths splendid, and-clothed-in-them for-him, and-set-out, he-and-him, to the-judge, and-declared upon his-self that-he his-son.
sentences.i: Then the cook went down to the market and bought Badr al-Dīn splendid garments, and dressed him in them, and went with him to the judge, and publicly declared, on his own account, that the boy was his son.
sentences.n: وَإِيَّاهُ, “and him”, is the idiom for “he and he together”: they set out together. أَشْهَرَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ is to make a public declaration binding oneself; the adoption is put on the judge's record.

sentences.t: وَقَدِ اشْتَهَرَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ فِي مَدِينَةِ دِمَشْقَ أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ الطَّبَّاخِ وَقَعَدَ عِنْدَهُ فِى الدُّكَّانِ يَقْبِضُ الدَّرَاهِمَ وَقَدِ اسْتَقَرَّ حَالُهُ عِنْدَ الطَّبَّاخِ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qadi ishtahara badru al-dīni ḥasanun fī madīnati dimashqa annahu waladu al-ṭabbākhi wa-qaʿada ʿindahu fī al-dukkāni yaqbiḍu al-darāhima wa-qadi istaqarra ḥāluhu ʿinda al-ṭabbākhi ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati
sentences.l: And-already became-known Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan in the-city-of Damascus that-he the-son-of the-cook, and-he-sat with-him in the-shop, taking the-dirhams; and-already settled his-state with the-cook upon this the-state.
sentences.i: And Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan became known throughout the city of Damascus as the cook's son, and he sat with him in the shop taking in the money; and so his condition settled, with the cook, upon this footing.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ بَدْرِ الدِّينِ حَسَنٍ وَمَا جَرَيٰ لَهُ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri badri al-dīni ḥasanin wa-mā jarā lahu
sentences.l: This is what was of the-affair-of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and-what happened to-him.
sentences.i: So much for the affair of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and what befell him.
sentences.n: جَرَيٰ is printed with a dotted ya, جري; read jarā, “happened”.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِسِتِّ الْحُسْنِ بِنْتِ عَمِّهِ فَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا طَلَعَ الْفَجْرُ وَانْتَبَهَتْ مِنَ النَّوْمِ لَمْ تَجِدْ بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amrisitti al-ḥusni binti ʿammihi fa-innahu lammā ṭalaʿa al-fajru wa-intabahat min al-nawmi lam tajid badra al-dīni ḥasana
sentences.l: And-as-for what was of the-affair-of-Sitt al-Ḥusn, daughter-of his-paternal-uncle: for-it-was, when rose the-dawn and-she-awoke from the-sleep, she-did-not find Badr-al-Dīn Ḥasan.
sentences.i: As for Sitt al-Ḥusn, his cousin: when dawn rose and she woke from sleep, she did not find Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan.
sentences.n: The print runs امر and ست together. سِتّ is “lady” and الْحُسْنِ is “beauty”: Sitt al-Ḥusn, “Lady of Beauty”. بِنْتِ عَمِّهِ, “daughter of his paternal uncle”, is how Arabic says “his cousin”. The name حَسَنَ is given a bare fatha as the object, since the print has no alif for a tanwīn.

sentences.t: فَاعْتَقَدَتْ أَنَّهُ دَخَلَ الْمِرْحَاضَ فَجَلَسَتْ تَنْتَظِرُهُ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-iʿtaqadat annahu dakhala al-mirḥāḍa fa-jalasat tantaẓiruhu sāʿatan
sentences.l: So-she-believed that-he had-entered the-privy, so-she-sat waiting-for-him an-hour.
sentences.i: She supposed he had gone into the privy, and sat waiting for him for an hour.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِأَبِيهَا قَدْ دَخَلَ وَهُوَ مَهْمُومٌ مِمَّا جَرَيٰ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ السُّلْطَانِ وَ كَيْفَ غَصَبَهُ وَزَوَّجَ ابْنَتَهُ غَصْبًا لِأَحَدِ غِلْمَانِهِ وَهُوَ قِطْعَةُ سَائِسٍ أَحْدَبَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-abīhā qad dakhala wa-huwa mahmūmun mimmā jarā ʿalayhi min al-sulṭāni wa kayfa ghaṣabahu wa-zawwaja ibnatahu ghaṣban li-aḥadi ghilmānihi wa-huwa qiṭʿatu sāʾisin aḥdaba
sentences.l: And-behold, with-her-father had entered, and-he grieved from-what happened upon-him from the-sultan, and how he-coerced-him and-married-off his-daughter by-force to-one-of his-slave-lads, and-he a-piece-of a-groom hunchbacked.
sentences.i: And behold, her father came in, grieving over what had befallen him at the sultan's hands: how the sultan had coerced him, and forced his daughter into marriage with one of his slave-lads, a lump of a hunchbacked groom.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِأَبِيهَا: the بِـ after إِذَا marks what suddenly appears, “and behold, her father”. The stray وَ before كَيْفَ is printed apart from its word. قِطْعَةُ سَائِسٍ, “a piece of a groom”, is contemptuous, “a lump of a groom”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ فِى نَفْسِهِ أَقْتُلُ هَذِهِ الْبِنْتَ إِنْ كَانَتْ مَكَّنَتْ هَذَا الْمَلْعُونَ مِنْ نَفْسِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla fī nafsihi aqtulu hādhihi al-binta in kānat makkanat hādhā al-malʿūna min nafsihā
sentences.l: And-he-said in his-self: I-kill this the-girl, if she-was she-gave-access to-this the-accursed from her-self.
sentences.i: And he said to himself, “I shall kill this girl, if she let that accursed creature have her.”
sentences.n: مَكَّنَهُ مِنْ نَفْسِهَا, “gave him power over her person”, means she yielded herself to him.

sentences.t: فَمَشَى إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى الْبَشْخَانَةِ وَوَقَفَ عَلَى بَابِهَا وَقَالَ يَاسِتَّ الْحُسْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-mashā ilā an waṣala ilā al-bashkhānati wa-waqafa ʿalā bābihā wa-qāla yā-sitta al-ḥusni
sentences.l: So-he-walked until he-arrived at the-bashkhāna, and-stood at its-door, and-said: O Sitt al-Ḥusn!
sentences.i: He walked on until he reached the inner chamber, stood at its door, and called, “Sitt al-Ḥusn!”
sentences.n: الْبَشْخَانَة (bashkhāna) is the room where bride and groom meet; the word is obscure, and "inner chamber" is a guess from context.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَبَّيْكَ يَاسَيِّدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu labbayka yā-sayyidī
sentences.l: So-she-said to-him: At-your-service, O-my-lord.
sentences.i: She answered, “At your service, my lord.”
sentences.n: لَبَّيْكَ is the formula for answering a summons: “here I am”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنَّهَا خَرَجَتْ وَهِيَ تَتَمَايَلُ مِنَ الْفَرَحِ وَ قَبَّلَتِ الْأَرْضَ وَزَادَ وَجْهُهَا نُورًا وَجَمَالًا بِعِنَاتِهَا ذَلِكَ الْغَزَالَ
sentences.tr: thumma annahā kharajat wa-hiya tatamāyalu min al-faraḥi wa qabbalati al-arḍa wa-zāda wajhuhā nūran wa-jamālan bi-ʿinātihā dhālika al-ghazāla
sentences.l: Then that-she went-out, and-she swaying from the-joy, and kissed the-earth, and-increased her-face in-light and-beauty through-her-ʿināt (sic) that the-gazelle.
sentences.i: Then she came out, swaying with joy, and kissed the ground, and her face grew in radiance and beauty from embracing that gazelle.
sentences.n: بِعِنَاتِهَا is obscure; I vocalise the letters as printed. A misprint for بِعِنَاقِهَا, “by her embracing”, would give the sense I translate, with الْغَزَال, “the gazelle”, her husband. Her kissing the ground is the courtesy due a father. The stray وَ is printed apart from its word.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَهَا أَبُوهَا وَهِيَ بِتِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ قَالَ لَهَا يَا مَلْعُونَةُ أَنْتِ فَرْحَانَةٌ بِهَذَا السَّائِسِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarahā abūhā wa-hiya bi-tilka al-ḥālati qāla lahā yā malʿūnatu anti farḥānatun bi-hādhā al-sāʾisi
sentences.l: So-when saw-her her-father, and-she in that the-state, he-said to-her: O accursed-one, you glad with-this the-groom!
sentences.i: When her father saw her in that state, he said to her, “Accursed girl! Are you glad of this groom?”
sentences.n: فَرْحَانَةٌ is the colloquial feminine of فَرْحَان, “glad”; Classical has فَرْحَى. The sentence has no question word; the question is in the tone.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ سِتُّ الْحُسْنِ كَلَامَ وَالِدِهَا تَبَسَّمَتْ وَقٰلَتْ بِاللَّهِ يَكْفِي مَا جَرَى أَمْسِ وَالنَّاسُ يَضْحَكُونَ عَلَيَّ وَيُعَايِرُونِي بِهَذَا السَّائِسِ الَّذِي مَا يَجِيئُ فِي قُلَامَةِ ظُفْرِ زَوْجِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat sittu al-ḥusni kalāma wālidihā tabassamat wa-qālat bi-Allāhi yakfī mā jarā amsi wa-al-nāsu yaḍḥakūna ʿalayya wa-yuʿāyirūnī bi-hādhā al-sāʾisi alladhī mā yajīʾu fī qulāmati ẓufri zawjī
sentences.l: So-when heard Sitt al-Ḥusn the-speech-of her-father, she-smiled and-said: By-God, suffices what happened yesterday, while the-people laugh upon me and-taunt-me with-this the-groom, who does-not come in a-paring-of the-nail-of my-husband.
sentences.i: When Sitt al-Ḥusn heard her father's words she smiled, and said, “By God, enough of what happened yesterday, with people laughing at me and taunting me with this groom, who is not worth a paring of my husband's fingernail.”
sentences.n: قلت is printed for قَالَتْ, “she said”, a defective spelling; the dagger alif shows the long vowel. يُعَايِرُونِي runs the plural ending -ūna and the pronoun -nī into -ūnī, a colloquial reduction. يَجِيئُ keeps the hamza-on-ya the print gives. مَا يَجِيئُ فِي, “does not come into”, is “does not amount to”.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ مَا بِتُّ طُولَ عُمْرِي لَيْلَةً أَحْسَنَ مِنْ لَيْلَةِ الْبَارِحَةِ فَلَا تَهْزَأْبِي وَتَذْكُرْلِي ذَلِكَ الْأَحْدَبَ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi mā bittu ṭūla ʿumrī laylatan aḥsana min laylati al-bāriḥati fa-lā tahzaʾbī wa-tadhkurlī dhālika al-aḥdaba
sentences.l: And-by-God, not I-spent-the-night, the-length-of my-life, a-night better than the-night-of the-last-night; so do-not mock-at-me and-mention-to-me that the-hunchback.
sentences.i: By God, in all my life I have never spent a better night than last night; so do not mock me, and do not bring up that hunchback to me.
sentences.n: تَهْزَأْبِي and وَتَذْكُرْلِي are each printed as one word: the verb fused with بِي, “at me”, and with لِي, “to me”. The second verb is a jussive carried on by فَلَا, “do not ... and mention”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ وَالِدُهَا كَلَامَهَا امْتَزَجَ بِالْغَضَبِ وَازْرَقَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa wāliduhā kalāmahā imtazaja bi-al-ghaḍabi wa-izraqqat ʿaynāhu
sentences.l: So-when heard her-father her-speech, he-was-mixed with-the-anger, and-turned-blue his-two-eyes.
sentences.i: When her father heard her words, he was steeped in rage, and his eyes turned blue.
sentences.n: Eyes turning blue is a stock sign of fury.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا وَيْلَكِ أَيْشَ هَذَا الْكَلَامُ الَّذِي تَقُولِيهِ السَّائِسُ الْأَحْدَبُ بَاتَ عِنْدَكِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā waylaki aysha hādhā al-kalāmu alladhī taqūlīhi al-sāʾisu al-aḥdabu bāta ʿindaki
sentences.l: And-he-said to-her: Woe-to-you! What this the-speech which you-say it? The-groom the-hunchback spent-the-night with-you?
sentences.i: He said to her, “Woe to you! What is this you are saying? The hunchbacked groom spent the night with you?”
sentences.n: ايش, “what”, is colloquial (from أَيُّ شَيْءٍ). تَقُولِيهِ has the colloquial ending -ī-hi where Classical has تَقُولِينَهُ. The last question has no question word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ لَا تَذْكُرْهُ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ أَبَاهُ وَلَا تَعْمَلْ مِزَاحَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat bi-Allāhi ʿalayka lā tadhkurhu laʿana Allāhu abāhu wa-lā taʿmal mizāḥa
sentences.l: So-she-said: By-God upon-you, do-not mention-him — cursed God his-father — and-do-not make jest.
sentences.i: She said, “By God, I beg you, do not speak of him — God curse his father — and do not make jokes.”
sentences.n: بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ, “by God, upon you”, is an adjuration. لَعَنَ اللَّهُ أَبَاهُ is a stock curse, the perfect used as a wish. مِزَاحَ has no printed alif, so I give it the bare fatha of the accusative.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَ السَّائِسُ إِلَّا مُكْرَي بِعَشَرَةِ دَنَانِيرَ وَأَخَذَ أُجْرَتَهُ وَرَاحَ
sentences.tr: fa-mā kāna al-sāʾisu illā mukrā bi-ʿasharati danānīra wa-akhadha ujratahu wa-rāḥa
sentences.l: For not was the-groom except a-hired-one for ten dinars, and-he-took his-wage and-went-off.
sentences.i: The groom was nothing but a hireling, engaged for ten dinars; he took his wage and went off.
sentences.n: مُكْرَى, “hired”, is printed with a dotted ya, مكري; I read it as the passive participle, with the dagger alif for the final long vowel.

sentences.t: وَجِئْتُ أَنَا وَدَخَلْتُ الْبَشْخَانَةَ فَنَظَرْتُ زَوْجِي قَاعِدًا بَعْدَ مَا جَلَوْنِي عَلَيْهِ الْمَغَانِي
sentences.tr: wa-jiʾtu anā wa-dakhaltu al-bashkhānata fa-naẓartu zawjī qāʿidan baʿda mā jalawnī ʿalayhi al-maghānī
sentences.l: And-I-came, I, and-entered the-bashkhāna, and-saw my-husband sitting, after-what they-displayed-me to-him, the-singing-women.
sentences.i: Then I came and went into the inner chamber, and saw my husband sitting there, after the singing-women had displayed me to him.
sentences.n: جَلَوْنِي عَلَيْهِ الْمَغَانِي has the plural verb before its plural subject, “they displayed me, the singing-women”, a colloquial agreement. جَلَا is to display a bride to her bridegroom.

sentences.t: وَنَقَّطَ بِالذَّهَبِ الْأَحْمَرِ حَتَّى أَغْنَى الْفُقَرَأَ الْحَاضِرِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-naqqaṭa bi-al-dhahabi al-aḥmari ḥattā aghnā al-fuqarāʾa al-ḥāḍirīna
sentences.l: And-he-showered with-the-gold the-red, until he-enriched the-poor the-present.
sentences.i: And he showered them with red gold, until he had made rich the poor who were present.
sentences.n: نَقَّطَ بِالذَّهَبِ is to scatter gold, as wedding-guests are showered with coin. The verb has no stated subject; it can only be the bridegroom, and I translate it so.

sentences.t: وَقَدْبِتُّ فِي حِضْنِ زَوْجِي الْخَفِيفِ صَاحِبِ الْعُيُونِ السُّودِ وَالْحَوَاجِبِ الْمَقْرُونَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qadbittu fī ḥiḍni zawjī al-khafīfi ṣāḥibi al-ʿuyūni al-sūdi wa-al-ḥawājibi al-maqrūnati
sentences.l: And-already I-spent-the-night in the-bosom-of my-husband, the-light, owner-of the-eyes the-black and-the-eyebrows the-joined.
sentences.i: And I have spent the night in the arms of my husband, the nimble, charming one, with the black eyes and the joined eyebrows.
sentences.n: الْخَفِيفِ, “light”, praises him as agile and charming. Eyebrows that meet over the nose, الْحَوَاجِبِ الْمَقْرُونَةِ, were admired as beautiful. The print fuses وَقَدْ with بِتُّ.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ وَالِدُهَا هَذَا الْكَلَامَ صَارَ الضِّيَاءُ فِي وَجْهِهِ ظَلَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa wāliduhā hādhā al-kalāma ṣāra al-ḍiyāʾu fī wajhihi ẓalāma
sentences.l: So-when heard her-father this the-speech, became the-light in his-face darkness.
sentences.i: When her father heard this speech, the light in his face turned to darkness.
sentences.n: ظَلَام has no printed alif, so the accusative after صَارَ is given only a bare fatha. الضِّيَاءُ and ظَلَام are set against each other as light and dark.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا فَاجِرَةُ مَا هَذَا الَّذِي تَقُولِيهِ أَيْنَ عَقْلُكِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā yā fājiratu mā hādhā alladhī taqūlīhi ayna ʿaqluki
sentences.l: And-he-said to-her: O wanton, what this which you-say it? Where your-mind?
sentences.i: He said to her, “You shameless woman, what is this you are saying? Where is your mind?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا أَبَتِ لَقَدْ فَتَّتْتَ كَبِدِي فَبَسْكَ تَنْتَاقَلُ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu yā abati laqad fattatta kabidī fa-basaka tantāqalu ʿalayya
sentences.l: So-she-said to-him: O my-father, you-have crumbled my-liver; so enough-of-you, you-are-heavy upon-me.
sentences.i: She said to him, “Father, you have broken my heart. Enough! You are being a burden to me.”
sentences.n: The liver is the seat of feeling, so “you have crumbled my liver” is “you have torn at my heart”. فَبَسْكَ is colloquial بَسّ, “enough”, with the pronoun -ka. تَنْتَاقَلُ is obscure; the letters suggest تَتَثَاقَلُ or تَتَنَاقَلُ, and I take it as “you weigh heavily upon me”.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا زَوْجِى الَّذِي أَخَذَ وَجْهِي قَدْ دَخَلَ إِلَى بَيْتِ الرَّاحَةِ وَإِنِّي قَدْ عَلِقْتُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā zawjī alladhī akhadha wajhī qad dakhala ilā bayti al-rāḥati wa-innī qad ʿaliqtu minhu
sentences.l: So-this my-husband, who took my-face, has entered to the-house-of the-rest, and-I have conceived from-him.
sentences.i: Here is my husband, who has taken me, gone into the privy; and I have conceived by him.
sentences.n: اخذ وجهي, “took my face”, is an idiom I cannot place with confidence; I take it as “took me”, the face standing for the person. بَيْتِ الرَّاحَةِ, “house of ease”, is the privy. عَلِقَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ is said of a woman conceiving.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ وَالِدُهَا وَهُوَ مُتَعَجِّبٌ وَدَخَلَ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْخَلَاءِ فَوَجَدَ السَّائِسَ الْأَحْدَبَ رَأْسُهُ مَغْرُوزَةٌ فِى الْمَلَاقِي وَرِجْلَيْهِ إِلَى فَوْقُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma wāliduhā wa-huwa mutaʿajjibun wa-dakhala ilā bayti al-khalāʾi fa-wajada al-sāʾisa al-aḥdaba raʾsuhu maghrūzatun fī al-malāqī wa-rijlayhi ilā fawqu
sentences.l: So-rose her-father, and-he amazed, and-entered to the-house-of the-emptiness, and-found the-groom the-hunchback, his-head stuck in the-throwing-places, and-his-two-legs to above.
sentences.i: Her father got up in amazement and went into the privy, and there he found the hunchbacked groom with his head stuck in the pit and his legs in the air.
sentences.n: الْمَلَاقِي is obscure; I take it as the plural of مَلْقًى, “a place where things are thrown”, here the privy-pit. رِجْلَيْهِ has the oblique dual ending where Classical would have the nominative رِجْلَاهُ. بَيْتِ الْخَلَاءِ, “house of the empty place”, is another word for the privy.

sentences.t: فَبَهِتَ فِيهِ الْوَزِيرُ وَقَالَ مَا هَذَا إِلَّا هُوَالْأَحْدَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-bahita fīhi al-wazīru wa-qāla mā hādhā illā huwa al-aḥdabu
sentences.l: So-was-stupefied at-him the-vizier, and-said: Not this except he the-hunchback.
sentences.i: The vizier stared at him, dumbfounded, and said, “This can be none other than the hunchback.”
sentences.n: هُوَالْأَحْدَبُ is printed as one word, “he, the hunchback”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَحْدَبُ فَقَالَ تَغُومْ تَغُومْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā aḥdabu fa-qāla taghūm taghūm
sentences.l: So-he-said to-him: O hunchback! So-he-said: taghūm, taghūm.
sentences.i: He said to him, “Hunchback!” and the other said, “Taghūm, taghūm.”
sentences.n: تَغُومْ is not a word I can identify. It may be a slurring of تَقُومْ, “you rise”, with غ for ق, but it reads best as the terrified gabble of the man in the pit, who thinks he is being addressed by a spirit. I keep it as printed.

sentences.t: فَظَنَّ الْأَحْدَبُ أَنَّهُ مَايُكَلِّمُهُ إِلَّا الْعِفْرِيتُ
sentences.tr: fa-ẓanna al-aḥdabu annahu māyukallimuhu illā al-ʿifrītu
sentences.l: So-thought the-hunchback that-he not-speaks-to-him except the-ifrit.
sentences.i: The hunchback thought that none but the ifrit could be speaking to him.
sentences.n: عِفْرِيت is a powerful, often malignant, spirit. As his next words show, the hunchback takes the vizier for the chief of the ifrits, whom he blames for putting him in the pit. مَايُكَلِّمُهُ is مَا يُكَلِّمُهُ run together.

sentences.t: فَعَيَّطَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَزِيرُ وَقَالَ تَكَلَّمْ وَإِلَّا قَطَعْتُ رَأْسَكَ بِهَذَا السَّيْفِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿayyaṭa ʿalayhi al-wazīru wa-qāla takallam wa-illā qaṭaʿtu raʾsaka bi-hādhā al-sayfi
sentences.l: So-he-shouted at-him, the-vizier, and-said: Speak, and-if-not I-cut-off your-head with-this the-sword.
sentences.i: The vizier shouted at him, “Speak, or I will cut off your head with this sword!”
sentences.n: عَيَّطَ عَلَيْهِ is colloquial, “to shout at”. وَإِلَّا قَطَعْتُ is “or else I have cut”: the perfect makes the threat sound as good as done.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ الْأَحْدَبُ وَاللَّهِ يَا شَيْخَ الْعَفَارِيتِ مِنْ حِينِ جَعَلْتَنِي فِي هَذَا الْمَكَانِ مَا رَفَعْتُ رَأْسِي فَبِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ ارْفُقْ بِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qāla al-aḥdabu wa-Allāhi yā shaykha al-ʿafārīti min ḥīni jaʿaltanī fī hādhā al-makāni mā rafaʿtu raʾsī fa-bi-Allāhi ʿalayka irfuq bī
sentences.l: So at that said the-hunchback: By-God, O chief-of the-ifrits, from the-time you-put-me in this the-place I-have-not raised my-head; so by-God upon-you, be-gentle with-me.
sentences.i: Then the hunchback said, “By God, chief of the ifrits, from the moment you put me in this place I have not lifted my head. By God, I beg you, be gentle with me.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ كَلَامَ الْأَحْدَبِ قَالَ لَهُ مَا تَقُولُ فَأَنَا أَبُو الْعَرُوسَةِ مَا أَنَا عِفْرِيتٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru kalāma al-aḥdabi qāla lahu mā taqūlu fa-anā abū al-ʿarūsati mā anā ʿifrītun
sentences.l: So-when heard the-vizier the-speech-of the-hunchback, he-said to-him: What do-you-say? For-I the-father-of the-bride; not I an-ifrit.
sentences.i: When the vizier heard the hunchback's words he said to him, “What are you saying? I am the bride's father; I am no ifrit.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَسْكَ فَأَنْتَ رَابِحٌ تَأْخُذُ رُوحِي فَرُحْ إِلَى حَلِّ سَبِيلِكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكَ الَّذِي فَعَلَ مَعِي هَذِهِ الْفِعَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla basaka fa-anta rābiḥun taʾkhudhu rūḥī fa-ruḥ ilā ḥalli sabīlika qabla an yaʾtiyaka alladhī faʿala maʿī hādhihi al-fiʿāla
sentences.l: So-he-said: Enough-of-you! For-you a-gainer, you-take my-soul. So-go to the-loosing-of your-way, before comes-to-you the-one-who did with-me these the-deeds.
sentences.i: He said, “Enough! You are about to take my life. Go on your way, before the one who did these things to me comes for you.”
sentences.n: رَابِحٌ is “gaining, profiting”, which sits oddly with تَأْخُذُ رُوحِي. I suspect a misprint for رَايِح, Egyptian “going to” (rāyiḥ taʾkhud, “you are about to take”), and translate so. فَرُحْ is the colloquial imperative of رَاحَ, “go”; حَلِّ سَبِيلِكَ, “the loosing of your way”, is “be off”.

sentences.t: فَأَنْتُمْ مَا جِبْتُمْ تُزَوِّجُونِي إِلَّا بِمَعْشُوقَةِ الْجَوَامِيسِ وَمَعْشُوقَةِ الْعَفَارِيتِ
sentences.tr: fa-antum mā jibtum tuzawwijūnī illā bi-maʿshūqati al-jawāmīsi wa-maʿshūqati al-ʿafārīti
sentences.l: For-you not brought, you-marry-me, except to the-beloved-of the-buffaloes and-the-beloved-of the-ifrits.
sentences.i: For all you did was bring me here to marry me to the sweetheart of buffaloes and the sweetheart of ifrits.
sentences.n: مَا جِبْتُمْ is colloquial, “you brought” (Classical جِئْتُمْ بِ), with the following verb giving the purpose: “you brought (me) to marry me”. زَوَّجَهُ بِ is “to marry someone to”. The bride is abused as the lover of buffaloes and demons.

sentences.t: فَلَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ زَوَّجَنِي بِهَا وَلَعَنَ مَنْ كَانَ السَّبَبَ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-laʿana Allāhu man zawwajanī bi-hā wa-laʿana man kāna al-sababa fīhā
sentences.l: So-cursed God whoever married-me to-her, and-cursed whoever was the-cause in-it.
sentences.i: So may God curse whoever married me to her, and whoever was the cause of it.
sentences.n: The perfect laʿana is a curse-formula, “may He curse”. فِيهَا is “in it”, that is, in the affair.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿan al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And-overtook Shahrazād the-morning, so-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving off the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The formula that closes each night: dawn catches Shahrazād and she stops, with الصَّبَاحُ and الْمُبَاحِ as the rhyme. الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ is “permitted speech”, talk that is lawful to continue.
